stories.title: Yogi questions, 'If your vehicle has petrol, why queue up?':Warns people against spreading rumours of lockdowns
stories.summary: 'What kind of low-level efforts are being made to stop Modi? What rumors are being spread? They are saying there will be a lockdown. It is our duty that if a cylinder lasts 25 days, why are we standing in line on the 5th day? When the car has full petrol, then why are we standing in line? We must be cautious and alert about these rumour-mongers. When the country's leadership is with you, why are you worried? The public has evicted them from the government, and now they are spreading rumours. Spreading rumours is also treason.' CM Yogi said this in Lucknow on Sunday. He distributed joining letters to selected nursing officers of Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences at Lok Bhavan at 4:30 PM. A total of 665 nursing officers have been selected. This includes 345 male and 320 female candidates. CM Yogi handed over joining letters directly to 20 candidates. Online joining letters will be sent to the remaining candidates. Yogi said that the results of the transparent appointment process are in front of everyone. We gave government jobs to 9 lakh candidates. Even opponents cannot question the selection process. Due to transparent appointments, there is no court intervention in this. Now read CM Yogi's important statements Everyone knows what happens to those who create irregularities Yogi says, 'Before 2017, most recruitments were hindered. With 9 lakh manpower, UP has transformed from a sick state to the country's growth engine. The state that didn't have money even for salaries is now a revenue surplus state. Today, our per capita income has tripled. There is no interference in recruitment exams. Appointment letters are distributed every week. The recruitment commission is under the third eye of the government. No irregularities should occur. Everyone knows what happens to those who try to mess with the future of youth - they are caught before they can cause any damage'. 1 lakh jobs will be created from Jewar Airport CM says, ‘We have built the biggest airport in UP yesterday. Our state is the biggest, so we will do the biggest work too. One lakh youth will get employment. Earlier, Jewar was the biggest crime center in the state. No one used to pass through there in the evening’. Today, we have made it the biggest investment center. A film city is being built there. The foundation stone of the semiconductor unit has also been laid near it. There was a time when people became helpless without oil; now they become helpless without semiconductors. Rumors of lockdown are being spread Yogi said that the world is in crisis, and there is an atmosphere of turmoil and doubt. Many countries have reduced working hours. Even in America, petrol prices are touching the sky. Our neighboring countries are also in bad condition. But, India is moving forward without stopping. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has reduced excise duty on petrol and diesel. All sections are benefiting from this. Rumors of lockdown are being spread in the country. Distribution of appointment letters every week is the result of our work CM says, ‘Zero tolerance is not only against crime and criminals. There is also zero tolerance towards corruption. The government has been working towards the goal of zero corruption since day one. As a result, every week we are involved in some appointment letter distribution program’. Akhilesh didn't visit Noida while being CM, but reached there today CM said that Akhilesh didn't visit Noida while being Chief Minister, but today reached there for divisive politics. The JPNIC building was built in the name of Jai Prakash Narayan. Its DPR was ₹200 crores, but ₹800 crores were spent on it. It's still incomplete. This is SP's development model. How dare they talk about development? They have no shame. Gomti River Front had a DPR of ₹300 crores, and ₹1400 crores were spent. Still, it remains incomplete. This is a robbery of the public's hard-earned money. As soon as jobs were announced, they would start collecting bribes. Today, even a Yadav daughter from Amethi got selected. But, she couldn't have been selected before 2017. Because her family couldn't pay money. I have already said that if any mistake is found, I will make such an example that it will become a precedent. Yogi gave joining letters to these candidates Those who received joining letters from CM Yogi include Priyanka Singh, Manish Kumar, Lakshman Ram Chaudhary, Mohammad Alam, Tanu, Sandhya Joshi, Devraj Gurjar, Devesh Kumar, Jai Prakash Singh, Dharmendra Kajla, Kumari Anamika Yadav, Deepti Devi, Pratima Kashyap, Akanksha, Rishi Raj Gautam, Aradhya Singh, Priyanka Chaudhary, Vivek Kumar Gond, Sandhya Singh and Sharima Siddiqui. According to the Health Department, these appointments will increase the nursing staff in the government hospitals of the state. This will facilitate patient treatment. The quality of services will improve. Lohia Hospital Director Dr. CM Singh said that 42,280 applications were received. Exams were conducted in 34 cities across 14 states. Out of these, 665 were selected. Minister of State for Medical Education Mayankeshwar Sharan Singh said that Lohia Institute is the largest after PGI. The more blessings you receive from patients, the more meaningful your entry into this profession will be. Deputy CM said, ‘Jewar Airport caused pain to brother’ Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak said that you all are joining a big institution. How did UP bring change? What were the conditions here before 2017? Could our daughters go out safely in the evening? Jobs were also given based on the brother-nephew's recommendations. For jobs, one had to make rounds from Etawah to Saifai for the brother-nephew's favor. Parents had to sell jewelry and land for jobs. Now, no one has asked for even 25 paise from anyone. I didn't even ask the director when the exam is happening. Which agency is it, because whoever asks will go to jail. See what the police did to the person who molested a 7-year-old daughter in Agra - this is the power of your vote. You need to tell the public that UP has the lotus, BJP, and CM Yogi. Only then is the state secure. UP is in safe hands today, in Yogi ji's hands. This white coat is a symbol of peace. The brother got hurt at the Jewar airport. stories.title: Akhilesh says, 'Noida Airport inaugurated to be sold':SP Chief adds, 'Those who never faced oppression can’t understand our pain'
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav addressed the Samajwadi Samta Bhaichara Rally in Dadri, Noida, on Sunday. Taking a jibe at the inauguration of Jewar Airport, he said that 6 out of 7 airports in UP have been closed. They could have at least promised that it would not be sold after the inauguration. It seems that this inauguration was done only to sell it. He says, ‘Those who have not endured the pain of atrocities, injustice, and oppression cannot understand our pain. They can show sympathy, but they cannot feel the pain that we felt when our house was washed with Gangajal’. SP chief said; We felt this pain when temples were washed after our visit. We don't want to destroy those negative people, we just want to make them understand. Times have changed now. There is still time - stop the trickery, stop the discrimination. The future is not theirs. Otherwise, just as their flags have come down today, tomorrow they will be removed from the throne of power. Earlier, Akhilesh paid floral tributes to the statue of Emperor Mihir Bhoj of the 9th-century Gurjar-Pratihar dynasty. After that, he purified his statue with Gangajal. This rally is being considered as the beginning of SP's 2027 assembly election campaign. Actually, the Gurjar community is considered quite influential in western UP. There are about 20,000 to 70,000 Gurjar votes in about 24 seats, like Ghaziabad, Noida, Dadri, Meerut, Muzaffarnagar, Saharanpur, Bijnor, Sambhal, and Kairana. Till now, it has been supporting the BJP. Now, SP wants to make inroads into this alliance. Key points from Akhilesh’s speech: 1. Our people exposed the truth of yesterday’s rally Akhilesh said that many of their workers have exposed the reality of yesterday’s rally. “No one can escape the camera. A party that calls itself the world’s largest had to rely on government employees. Now BJP’s exit from Uttar Pradesh is certain, and after that, from Delhi as well. We have not been in power for 10 years, at least they could have accounted for their smaller ‘ATM’. This ‘ATM’ must have troubled the entire world.” 2. No one can forget the Samajwadis’ contribution to Noida’s development “We fought when others tried to take away our history and our emperors. Form the government in 2027, and we will install statues of PDA icons at the riverfront in Lucknow to honour their contributions. No one can forget the Samajwadi Party’s role in Noida’s development. This is not just a rally, but a call to bring social justice to power in the coming time.” SP leaders honoured Akhilesh on stage. 3. We must bring change, no matter how long it takes “People of PDA know and feel discrimination and disrespect. Their dignity is taken away from time to time. We must bring change, whether it takes years or even a century; we will not step back. Five per cent of people are exploiting 95 per cent and depriving them of their rights.” 4. The Constitution will remain under threat as long as BJP exists “Babasaheb gave us a document stronger than an iron sword. No matter the obstacles, we will continue to fight to end inequality. For PDA, protecting the Constitution is a matter of life and death. Those who aimed to change the Constitution by winning 400 seats went underground after losing in 2024, but the Constitution will remain in danger as long as the BJP exists.” Before his address, Akhilesh was honoured with a turban on stage. 5. Jobs have never been part of BJP’s agenda Akhilesh said jobs have never been on the BJP’s agenda. “Reservation under Babasaheb Ambedkar’s Constitution has never been part of their agenda. That is why they do not provide government jobs and instead allow exam papers to leak.” 6. Samajwadi Party secured NOC for Jewar Airport “If anyone secured the NOC for Jewar Airport, it was the Samajwadi Party. That is why the airport has been built today. In the future, we will buy farmers’ land at market rates and ensure their respect.” He added that in the coming time, they will strengthen the 1090 helpline to ensure women’s safety, restart the Samajwadi Pension scheme, and provide ₹40,000 annually to poor women to support and empower them.

stories.title: ‘Madam, my followers are in lakhs, you can’t answer’:Truck driver threatens woman ARTO in Unnao,
stories.summary: A truck driver in Unnao threatened a female ARTO officer, saying he had millions of followers on social media and she would face consequences if she could not respond. The incident took place late on Saturday night when ARTO Pratibha Gautam and her team were checking overloaded vehicles. During the checking drive in the Dahi police station area, about 10 km from the district headquarters, the team stopped five vehicles and took them to a weighbridge for inspection. However, the GPS of the truck at the front got locked, which caused other trucks standing behind to get stuck as well. This led to delays and tension at the spot. Angered by the delay, one of the truck drivers started creating a ruckus. A constable from the checking team got into an argument with him. It is alleged that during the argument, a constable from the enforcement team caught the driver by his collar and started beating him. Seeing the commotion escalate, the female ARTO got out of the vehicle. It is being said that instead of stopping the constable, she herself started pushing the driver. Accusing him of drinking alcohol, she forcibly started putting him in the vehicle. At this, the truck driver got agitated. The enforcement team took him to the Dahi police station and handed him over to the police. The enforcement team says, ‘truck driver was under the influence of alcohol and violating rules’. Meanwhile, the driver alleges that he was forcibly stopped and assaulted. See 3 pictures Now read what the ARTO said According to ARTO Enforcement Pratibha Gautam, between 9:00 and 9:30 PM on Saturday night, she was checking for overloading near a factory in the Dahi police station area with her team. She was sitting in her government vehicle. Other members of the team were stopping and checking passing vehicles. The team stopped 5 overloaded trucks. All five trucks were taken to a weighbridge for overloading inspection. During weighing at the weighbridge, one truck's GPS got locked. Because of this, it stopped there. Then the truck drivers standing behind started creating a ruckus. Some of them were intoxicated. When a constable grabbed a truck driver's collar, she went to intervene, but the truck driver started misbehaving with her too, while making a video with his mobile. He started threatening her with consequences, claiming to be a social media influencer. Therefore, he was taken into custody and handed over to the police of Dahi police station. Police Station in charge said - Action will be taken upon receiving a complaint Dahi Police Station In-charge Gyanendra Singh said; The matter reached the police station late Saturday night. But so far, we have not received any complaint. The viral video has come to our attention. Further action will be taken only after receiving a complaint.

stories.title: 30 houses being demolished in Varanasi Dalmandi:Houses razed with chisels and hammers; 150 police personnel deployed, drone surveillance
stories.summary: Around 30 houses are being demolished in Dalmandi, Varanasi, on Sunday. Workers are using chisels and hammers to bring down the structures. More than 150 police personnel have been deployed, with barricades in place and movement in the area restricted. Surveillance is being carried out using drone cameras. According to the administration, all the properties have been registered, and compensation has been transferred to the stakeholders’ accounts. The action had earlier been paused due to Eid. Before this, 22 dilapidated houses had already been demolished. Dalmandi Street is set to be developed as a model road. The Prime Minister laid the foundation stone during his 51st visit to Kashi. The state government has sanctioned ₹215.88 crore for the project, with ₹191 crore allocated as compensation to 186 property owners. PWD officials said the 650-metre stretch from New Road to Chowk police station will be widened to 60 feet, including a 30-foot road and 15-foot footpaths on both sides. Power lines, sewerage and water systems will be moved underground, clearing the existing tangle of overhead wires. Pictures of action in Dalmandi...

stories.title: Man killed in Varanasi for informing on cattle smugglers:Dragged out of home, beaten to death with kicks and punches
stories.summary: A youth was beaten to death in Varanasi after being accused of mobile theft. The attackers barged into his house at midnight, dragged Sanu Ali out of his room and took him outside the village, where they assaulted him. They kept beating him with kicks and punches until he fell unconscious. Family members chased the attackers and reached the spot. They took him in a critical condition to Heritage Hospital, where he died during treatment in the morning. The accused fled after the incident. The police were informed during the night, but Rohanian police allegedly remained negligent in taking action. Family alleges prior threats Sanu Ali’s uncle Akhtar Ali said that Sanu had informed the police about Bablu and his associates involved in cattle smuggling. The accused first threatened him and later took him from his house and killed him. Angry family members questioned the police action and demanded immediate arrests. The incident is from Rohania Panditpur village. Attack inside home, brutal beating outside The attackers created a commotion at Sanu’s home, accusing him of mobile phone theft. They then claimed they were taking him to the police station but instead took him outside the village near a petrol pump and tied him to a small bridge, where they mercilessly beat him. By the time family members reached the spot, Sanu had already died. The family alleged that the police at the scene asked the attackers to take him for medical treatment instead of taking immediate action against them.

stories.title: No direct FIR in dowry harassment cases in UP:DGP order after High Court strictness; registration stopped in 31 cases
stories.summary: People in Uttar Pradesh will now see a major change in how some cases are reported. Police will not directly register FIRs in 31 types of cases, including dowry harassment and cheque bounce. Instead, people will first have to approach a magistrate and file a complaint in court. This decision comes after strong remarks by the Allahabad High Court in a recent case. Following this, DGP Rajiv Krishna has issued strict orders to all police officers across the state to follow the rule. Why has this rule been introduced The DGP said that in some offences, the law clearly says that only a direct complaint in court is allowed. In such cases, registering an FIR at the police station is not correct and is considered illegal. What will police do now Police officers will now have to carefully check each case before registering an FIR. The station in charge and the investigating officer must ensure whether the court can legally take action based on a police report. What does this mean for people People will now need to follow a legal process for certain cases. They cannot go directly to the police station for FIR registration in these matters. Instead, they must first file a complaint before a magistrate. The new rule aims to ensure that legal procedures are followed properly and to prevent incorrect FIR registrations. In these cases, FIR will not be registered now The circular issued by the DGP also includes a list of cases sent by the prosecution department, in which an FIR cannot be directly registered. These include cases related to domestic violence against women, dowry harassment, cheque bounce, female feticide, cruelty to animals, environment and pollution. Apart from these, in cases of consumer fraud and food adulteration, one will have to approach the Consumer Forum or FSSAI. The police will not register an FIR for this. Even in cases of child labor, air pollution, import/export of goods, trademarks, human organ trafficking, sexual harassment of women at the workplace, water pollution, cable television networks, foreign exchange management, and controlling pesticide drugs, an FIR will not be registered directly. For this, a complaint must first be registered with the concerned department. Why was this decision taken? The Allahabad High Court recently commented that sometimes the police register FIRs contrary to the rules. This benefits the accused in court. The entire investigation process gets wasted. Often, the victim does not get justice. DGP Rajiv Krishna also issued a warning through a circular. He said that if any police officer violates these instructions, departmental action will be taken against them. He has instructed all station in-charges and investigators to seriously study every aspect of the law. Before registering an FIR, make sure that it is not a case falling under the complaint category. What is the provision for punishment in cases of dowry harassment? According to the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, those who give, take, or abet the giving or taking of dowry can be imprisoned for up to 5 years. There is also a provision for a fine of Rs 15,000. For assault or demanding valuable items for dowry, punishment is given under Section 498A of the IPC. This entails 3 years of imprisonment and a fine. If the husband and in-laws refuse to hand over 'Stridhan' (woman's property), then there is a provision for both 3 years of imprisonment and a fine.

stories.title: From Dadri rally, Akhilesh to kick off Mission 2027:Focus on Gurjar vote bank; effect expected on 24 seats in West UP
stories.summary: SP chief Akhilesh Yadav will hold a 'Samajwadi Samta Bhaichara Rally' in Noida Dadri on Sunday. This is considered to be the beginning of SP's 2027 assembly election campaign. The question is, why did Akhilesh Yadav choose Noida to start his election campaign? Actually, the Gurjar vote is very important in Western UP. So far, it has supported the BJP. Now SP wants to breach this alliance. So, is this a strategy to compensate for the lack of Jayant Chaudhary with the Gurjar vote bank? Will the Gurjar community really come with SP? In this report, we will try to find answers to these questions Gurjars strong on 24 seats in Western UP The Gurjar community is considered very influential in Western UP. There are 20 to 70 thousand Gurjar votes on about 24 seats like Ghaziabad, Noida, Dadri, Meerut, Muzaffarnagar, Saharanpur, Bijnor, Sambhal, Kairana. Lok Sabha Elections 2024 Since 2014, this has been the core vote of the BJP. But, the SP wants to break it with a Muslim-Gurjar alliance. This is why the SP is focusing on the Gurjar vote bank along with backward, Dalit, and minority votes in its rallies. RLD vote bank did not shift to BJP in Lok Sabha The Samajwadi Party contested the 2022 assembly elections in alliance with Jayant Chaudhary's party, Rashtriya Lok Dal. However, before the Lok Sabha elections, Jayant allied with the BJP. Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar says - It did not have much effect in the Lok Sabha elections. RLD won in Bijnor and Baghpat, but its votes did not completely shift to BJP. This was the reason why the SP-Congress alliance won the Muzaffarnagar, Kairana, and Saharanpur seats, which are considered RLD strongholds. Now it's the assembly election. In such a situation, SP does not want to leave any stone unturned. It is starting from its weakest area. If SP's Gurjar leaders succeed in gathering a crowd there, this rally will increase lines of concern on the foreheads of both BJP and RLD. If SP gets even 20-25% Gurjar votes, the equations of many seats will change. Performance of SP-Congress in the Lok Sabha had surprised many In 2022, the RLD and SP alliance had an impact on several seats in Western UP. The SP-RLD alliance performed well in districts like Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Bijnor, Meerut, Saharanpur, Amroha, Moradabad, and Rampur. However, the alliance had to struggle considerably in districts like Bulandshahr, Noida, Ghaziabad, and Aligarh. After the election results, RLD separated from SP and joined BJP. In the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the SP-Congress alliance surprised everyone by winning 43 out of 80 seats in UP. Assembly Elections 2022 The SP-Congress alliance won seats like Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Saharanpur, Moradabad, Sambhal, and Rampur in Western UP. Meanwhile, the margin of defeat was very small on seats like Aligarh, Meerut, Farrukhabad, and Amroha. Akhilesh will test the strength of regional leaders with the rally Noida is the weakest link for SP. Akhilesh Yadav says that he is starting the campaign from the weakest region to assess the shortcomings of the organization as well as to gauge his influence in the Gurjar community. The entire focus of the rally is on the Gurjar community. Akhilesh Yadav wants to check how much truth there is in the claims made by Gurjar community leaders who come to Lucknow and assert that the entire community supports the Samajwadi Party. In fact, the SP has never been able to win the Dadri seat. Noida Seats History (SP Yet to Open Account) First the BSP and now the BJP are quite strong here. This is why when some leaders from Western UP asked Akhilesh if they also needed to bring people from their areas to the Dadri rally, Akhilesh's direct answer was - absolutely not. He said that he wants to test the leaders from that region who come to Lucknow and make big claims. Electoral atmosphere to be created by the BJP-SP rallies Prime Minister Narendra Modi had inaugurated Jewar International Airport on Saturday. While delivering his speech, he was aggressive towards SP. Now, on Sunday, Akhilesh Yadav is holding a rally in Dadri, Noida. It is obvious that he will target the BJP's central and UP governments. Akhilesh had targeted the Prime Minister by writing a post on X after the inauguration of Jewar Airport. After the inauguration of Jewar Airport and SP's rally, the issue of development versus ground reality will remain central. While on one hand, BJP is sending a message of development through large infrastructure projects, on the other hand, the opposition will try to raise ground-level problems and social equations by using these very projects as a basis. SP is calling the rally a brotherhood conference SP is not officially calling the Dadri rally an election campaign. Party's national spokesperson Ameek Jamei says - Western UP is important politically, because a large number of people from Jat and Gurjar communities live there. SP is going to hold a Brotherhood Conference. People from both sections will participate in large numbers. As far as the election campaign is concerned, the SP had started its campaign right after the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Akhilesh Yadav is continuously visiting districts. Meetings have also been held at some places. It is certain that this trend will increase as the elections draw closer.

stories.title: Crops on 4,300 hectares hit by unseasonal rain in UP:Yogi asks officers to visit fields, 4-day storm and rain warning
stories.summary: Unseasonal rains have caused heavy damage to crops in Uttar Pradesh over the past 15 days, affecting thousands of farmers across the state. According to the state government, crops spread across 4,300 hectares belonging to around 15,000 farmers have been damaged. Of this, 244.23 hectares were affected by hailstorms, while 4,053.11 hectares suffered damage due to heavy rainfall. So far, compensation has been given to 10,278 farmers. The remaining farmers are also being paid. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has asked officials to go to the field and assess the damage. He has also directed them to stay alert and speed up relief work. A new western disturbance is becoming active on Sunday. This will start a new spell of rain. It will begin in Western UP. Many districts will experience thundershowers. There is also a possibility of lightning strikes in some places. Good rainfall may begin across the entire state from tomorrow. There will be storms. Hail may also fall in some places. Regarding the temperature in the last 24 hours, Banda was the hottest at 39.8 degrees. Azamgarh was the coldest at 15.8 degrees. Lucknow's meteorologist Atul Singh said- Rainfall activities may intensify from the evening of March 29. Starting from West UP, the impact of rain will be seen across Central and East UP, including Lucknow. The weather will change rapidly with light to heavy rain in some places. Weather Pictures- How will the weather be for 3 days? March 30 - Light rain with thunder and lightning will occur across the entire state. Heavy rain may also occur in some places. A storm may also occur. March 31 - Showers will occur in Western UP. Eastern UP may experience good rainfall. Winds will blow at a speed of 30-40 km/h. April 1- There is a possibility of thundershowers across the entire state. Storms will occur. Hail may fall in some places. Warning of 60 km/h winds tomorrow Meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said - The weather in the state may worsen further on March 30. Strong winds may blow. The wind speed is likely to reach up to 60 kilometers per hour. In Eastern UP, winds may blow at a speed of 40 km per hour with thunder and lightning on March 30. Farmers affected by rain received compensation of ₹4.5 crore According to the UP government, relief assistance of ₹13.34 lakh has been provided to 286 farmers affected by hailstorms so far. Meanwhile, compensation of ₹4.47 crore has been given to 9,992 farmers affected by heavy rains. The damage to other affected individuals is being assessed. They will be provided relief soon.

stories.title: Jewar Airport becomes focus for Modi-Yogi:Target 108 seats, take dig at Akhilesh’s ‘Noida fear’, hail double engine government
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated Phase-1 of the Noida International Airport in Jewar on Saturday. During this, he made several significant statements regarding Western UP and SP chief Akhilesh Yadav. Akhilesh Yadav also retaliated against PM Modi. Behind this lies the political arithmetic of Western UP. In fact, Western UP has 108 assembly seats. The equation of Yadavs, Rajputs, Jat-Gurjars, and Muslims is quite important in this region. The first phase of the 2022 assembly elections also began in Western UP. Prime Minister Modi and Chief Minister Yogi crafted a new narrative of development from the airport in this very Western UP. Meanwhile, SP chief Akhilesh Yadav is participating in a large conference of Gurjars in Noida on March 29 (Sunday). He is also engaged in rectifying the political equations of Western UP. This is why, in the speeches of PM Modi and CM Yogi, only SP-Congress were targeted. BSP and other parties were not even mentioned in their speeches. The PM has given a big message by advising parties doing politics during Noida's superstition and the petroleum crisis, using the example of Corona. What are the political implications of PM Modi's 33-minute speech? How will BJP win back the stronghold of Western UP on the strength of sugarcane farmers and youth? Read in Dainik Bhaskar Analysis Development Timeline vs. Opposition's 'Obstruction' Senior journalist Ravindra Pratap Rana, who closely observes Western UP politics, says - PM Modi and CM Yogi presented Jewar Airport as a 'timeline success story'. Modi himself used Jewar Airport as an example to convey to the public why a double-engine government is necessary? Modi explained how between 2002-2017, the Congress government at the center and the SP government in the state left Western UP in a state of developmental limbo due to their incompetence. These governments did not even allow the foundation of Jewar Airport, which received approval in the Atal government in 2003, to be laid for years. In the initial two-three years of the NDA government formed at the center in 2014, the SP did not allow work on this. But as soon as the BJP government was formed in UP, the foundation of Jewar Airport was laid. The airport was built and now it has also been inaugurated. The meaning is clear, for the rapid development of the state, the BJP's double-engine government is necessary even in 2027. Attack on 'superstition': Attempt to break political myths PM Modi mentioned the old 'superstition' associated with Noida, where chief ministers hesitated to visit. When Modi first visited Noida after becoming PM in 2014, the then CM Akhilesh Yadav did not attend the event due to this superstition. Modi stated that attempts were made to scare him with this superstition as well. According to senior journalist Ravindra Pratap Rana, through this narrative, BJP achieved two objectives Before 2017, no CM of UP used to visit Noida. It was believed that whoever visited here would not become CM again. However, Yogi Adityanath broke this myth. By becoming CM again in 2022, he ended this perception. Attempt to cut caste equations with a development narrative The politics of Western UP has long revolved around Jat, Muslim, Gurjar, Yadav, and Dalit equations. The politics of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav and BJP ally Jayant Chaudhary rests on this social balance. After Jayant joined the BJP, Akhilesh Yadav has been trying to woo Jats and Gurjars in this belt. Whereas the BJP wants to cut this caste equation with a development narrative. Senior journalist Anand Rai says - PM Modi and CM Yogi did not mention Hindu-Muslim even once. Both leaders tried to convey the message that the development of this region is on their agenda by mentioning the development of Western UP and its major projects like Jewar Airport, Semiconductor Park, Namo Bharat, and Rapid Rail. Targeted youth by mentioning employment through investment A large number of youth participated in Modi's rally. PM Modi himself mentioned this from the stage. He then linked Jewar Airport to the dreams of the youth, explaining how various investments in this region would create numerous employment opportunities. The PM stated that currently, aircraft maintenance and repair are not done in the country. For this, one has to go abroad. Now, the MRO (Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul) facility being prepared near Jewar Airport will create large-scale employment. With Jewar becoming an international connectivity and cargo hub, investment is flowing into this region. Local industries and businesses will get access to the global market. This will also create a large number of employment opportunities. Modi showed his skill in connecting with the public Senior journalist Anand Rai says- Modi has once again proved why he has a strong hold on the public. He connects directly with people. This was also evident at Jewar Airport. When Modi addressed the public and said, "The inauguration is done." Then he himself said, "No, only half the work is done. I have only unveiled it." Then he asked the youth to take out their mobiles and turn on the flashlight. He said, "You inaugurate this airport by lighting a lamp. This is your trust. It is your future. It is your endeavor. Show the flashlight by saying 'Bharat Mata ki Jai'." The crowd did the same. The smiles visible on people's faces during this time clearly indicate that the PM succeeded in connecting with the public. Farmers integrated into the national economy Appreciating the farmers of Western UP, the PM said that the ethanol you produced from sugarcane has reduced dependence on crude oil. If ethanol production had not increased, the country would have had to import four and a half crore barrels (about 700 crore liters) of crude oil from abroad every year. The hard work of farmers has provided such great relief to the country in times of crisis. Ethanol has saved foreign exchange worth one and a half lakh crores. This money has gone to the farmers of the country. Friends, the sugarcane farmers here have also seen earlier days when sugarcane dues remained pending for many years. Today, due to the efforts of BJP's double engine government, the situation of sugarcane farmers has improved. On this, Anand Rai says- Sugarcane farmers in Western UP have always been a large vote bank. By ensuring timely payment for sugarcane and linking farmers producing ethanol from sugarcane to the national economy, the PM very skillfully tried to win over this vote bank. He directly credited the farmers who gave 13 thousand acres of land for Jewar Airport from the stage. Then, by making the crowd applaud in their support, he also conveyed the message of how much farmers have contributed to the country's progress. He also explained how, in the future, farmers will be able to earn significant profits by directly delivering their produce to the global market from Jewar Airport. Implications of the COVID-era advice on the petroleum crisis The PM also very clearly conveyed his message to the common people regarding the petroleum crisis. The PM said- In the situation of war happening in West Asia, we 140 crore Indians will have to face this crisis with patience and by maintaining unity. This is a crisis causing trouble in the world. We must prioritize our country's concerns. Modi also appealed to all political parties in the country not to repeat the COVID-era mistake. He said that in such a crisis, one should avoid making statements that are detrimental to the country. He also said that what is in the interest of Indians is the policy and strategy of the Government of India. Parties making wrong statements for politics might score some points in political debates. But the people of the country will never forgive actions that harm the nation. Even during the Corona period, some people similarly misled and lied, but the public rejected such politics during the elections. I am confident that the political parties of the country will learn a lesson from this and strengthen united efforts. Even during the COVID period, the opposition, including SP-Congress, created a lot of uproar, but in the subsequent assembly elections, the public rejected the opposition.

stories.summary: A massive fire broke out at the Yagya site of Uttar Pradesh Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh in Ayodhya on Saturday afternoon. The blaze erupted around 12 noon, reducing the one-acre Pandal to ashes within minutes. Fortunately, no casualties were reported as the site was empty at the time of the incident. Incident occurred shortly after Yagya conclusion The fire broke out nearly one and a half hours after the conclusion of a nine-day Lakshmi Narayan Mahayagna. At the time of the event’s conclusion, over 50,000 people were present. The site is located approximately 800 meters from the Ram Temple. Preliminary reports suggest that a spark generated while breaking a coconut after the ritual may have ignited the cloth Pandal. See pictures... Minister confirms situation under control Minister Dayashankar Singh stated that fire brigade teams were already present at the venue and responded immediately. “The fire was brought under control quickly. There has been no loss of life, and the situation is now under control,” he said. Narrow escape prevents major tragedy Eyewitnesses said the Yagya site had 1,251 Hawan Kunds, and on the final day, more than 5,000 devotees performed rituals. Most attendees had left after the ceremony concluded, which prevented what could have been a major tragedy. Had the Pandal been occupied, the incident could have resulted in significant casualties. Firefighters douse blaze after two-hour effort According to the Chief Fire Officer M.P. Singh, around 10 fire tenders were deployed, and it took nearly two hours to fully extinguish the fire. Officials confirmed that no injuries or casualties have been reported. Investigation underway Authorities are assessing the cause of the fire, though initial indications point to an accidental spark. Further investigation is ongoing.

stories.title: Ashutosh Brahmachari gets bomb threat from unknown number:Caller urges him to stop advocating against Shankaracharya
stories.summary: Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj, who filed an FIR against Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand over sexual abuse of minors, has received death threats. Brahmachari stated that an unknown caller warned him to stop advocating the case, saying: “Stop representing Shankaracharya’s case, or we will blow you up with a bomb. You and your lawyer Saurabh Gupta will be eliminated.” Following the threat, Brahmachari filed a complaint with Shamli police. After receiving the complaint, a police team visited his residence on Friday evening to record his statement. According to the complaint, on 25 March, an unknown number +92 320 0605681 made the threatening call. SSP Shamli Narendra Pratap Singh said that the matter is under investigation. Ashutosh Brahmachari is the advocate for the minors in the sexual abuse case against Swami Avimukteshwaranand. He had presented the children in court and filed the FIR at Jhunsi police station, Prayagraj. Meanwhile, the Allahabad High Court granted anticipatory bail to the Shankaracharya. Now read Ashutosh Maharaj's complaint... In the police complaint, Ashutosh Brahmachari said that he is the president of Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi Mukti Nirman Trust Mathura. He is the complainant in the case registered against Shankaracharya at Jhunsi police station in Prayagraj. A petition related to this case has also been filed in the Supreme Court. After filing a petition in the Supreme Court regarding Shankaracharya's case, he received a serious threat on his mobile/WhatsApp from an unknown person with mobile number +92 320 0605681. It was stated that if I pursue the above special leave petition or do not withdraw it, both myself and my advocate Saurabh Ajay Gupta will be blown up with a bomb. Shankaracharya approached Supreme Court after anticipatory bail was granted On 25 March, the Allahabad High Court granted anticipatory bail to Swami Avimukteshwaranand. The court ruled that the Shankaracharya would not be arrested until the chargesheet is filed. The court also prohibited Brahmachari from giving media interviews or making statements. The bench raised questions regarding the FIR, noting discrepancies: the victims reported the incident on 18 January, whereas Brahmachari filed it on 24 January. The court questioned why the children were not placed in proper custody immediately and why they first approached Brahmachari, whom they did not previously know. The court observed that the case and FIR must be carefully scrutinized to ensure it is not false. After the High Court granted anticipatory bail to Shankaracharya, Brahmachari approached the Supreme Court, seeking the Shankaracharya’s arrest. Now know the full matter There was a dispute between Shankaracharya and the administration on Mauni Amavasya on January 18 at the Prayagraj Magh Mela. 8 days later on January 24, Jagadguru Rambhadracharya's disciple Ashutosh Maharaj complained to the Police Commissioner. In this, allegations of sexual exploitation of children were made during Magh Mela-2026 and Mahakumbh-2025. Alleging inaction by police, a petition was filed in the Special POCSO Court on February 8. Two children were presented in court on February 13. Their statements were recorded on February 21. On the court's order, an FIR was registered at Jhunsi police station the same day. Shankaracharya, his disciple Mukundanand and 2-3 unknown accused were named in the FIR. On February 24, Shankaracharya accused Prayagraj Additional Commissioner Ajay Pal Sharma of conspiring against him. He also filed an anticipatory bail petition in the Allahabad High Court. On February 26, medical reports came in the sexual harassment case against Shankaracharya. Police sources claim that sexual abuse of children has been confirmed. Meanwhile, a victim Batuk came in front of the media for the first time. In an interview given to a channel, he claimed - I had gone for studies, that's when I was exploited.

stories.title: Fuel demand in Lucknow doubles in last 2 days:13 lakh cylinders booked in haste, officials claim no change in stock
stories.summary: Petrol, diesel and LPG demand suddenly surged across Uttar Pradesh, including Lucknow, on March 26–27, rising to two to three times the average. Triggered by rumours, the situation worsened, with petrol and diesel demand increasing by up to 100% (doubling). LPG cylinder bookings crossed 13 lakh. However, oil company officials said supply remains fully under control, with a standard seven-day stock available. Until March 24, petrol and diesel sales were following a normal trend, but from March 25, demand began to rise sharply. By March 26, the surge had peaked. Petrol (MS) sales were just 4% above average on March 24, but jumped to 38% on March 25 and 77% on March 26. Diesel (HSD) saw a sharper rise—from 19% on March 24 to 36% on March 25 and 75% on March 26. Over 100% surge in Lucknow Lucknow also saw a rapid change in the situation. Petrol sales rose from 3% above average on March 24 to 42% on March 25 and 109% on March 26. Diesel sales increased from 17% to 61% and then to 100% over the same period. Districts including Azamgarh, Barabanki, Bhadohi, Deoria, Gorakhpur, Kaushambi, Kushinagar, Pratapgarh, Prayagraj and Shravasti reported petrol sales rising between 170% and 222%. A similar trend was seen in diesel, with Deoria recording a 226% spike and Pratapgarh 230%. Maharajganj, Jaunpur, Gorakhpur and Azamgarh also recorded increases of over 170%. Along with petrol and diesel, LPG also saw a significant surge. On March 26, a total of 13.31 lakh cylinders were booked, while only 7.83 lakh could be delivered. Under Indian Oil, 5.25 lakh bookings were made against 4.32 lakh deliveries. Bharat Petroleum recorded 6.42 lakh bookings but only 2.11 lakh deliveries, while Hindustan Petroleum saw 1.64 lakh bookings and delivered 1.40 lakh cylinders. This created a backlog of around 5.5 lakh cylinders in a single day, which companies are now trying to clear quickly. Consumption doubled in 2 days Data shows that compared to March 26, 2025, petrol supply nearly doubled on March 26, 2026—from 15,000 kilolitres to 29,000 kilolitres (around 2.9 crore litres). Diesel followed the same trend, rising from 28,000 kilolitres to 51,000 kilolitres (around 5.01 crore litres). Some districts under pressure, situation improving now In districts like Lucknow, Sitapur, Bahraich and Gonda, demand pressure rose sharply. Meanwhile, conditions in Gorakhpur, Basti, Maharajganj and Ayodhya are gradually returning to normal. Officials said the situation in other districts is also expected to stabilise within one to two days. Supply system strong, stock sufficient There are around 13,000 petrol pumps in the state, each holding 4–5 days of stock. About 4,107 LPG distributors have an average stock of one and a half days, while bottling plants have around four days of stock. Overall, the system maintains a reserve of 15–18 days, which is considered normal. Officials' Appeal - Avoid Rumors UP coordinator for oil companies, Sanjay Bhandari, clarified that there is no shortage of petrol, diesel or LPG anywhere in the state. The supply chain is fully active and all demand is being met. People have been urged to avoid rumours and buy fuel only as needed. A seven-day backup stock is always maintained.

stories.title: Petrol spill after tanker crash triggers loot in Kanpur:Crowd gathers to collect petrol in drums, buckets; police clear area
stories.summary: A tanker loaded with petrol, which had broken down on the Gujaini elevated bridge in Kanpur, was hit by an unidentified vehicle. The strong impact damaged the tanker and petrol began leaking from it. The driver sought help from nearby people, but as soon as people came to know about the leaking petrol, chaos broke out on the highway. People rushed with drums and buckets to collect petrol. The driver immediately informed the police and company officials. Police reached the spot and took control of the situation, dispersing the crowd. After this, another tanker was called in the presence of the fire brigade and the process of transferring the petrol was started. As a safety measure, traffic was diverted by the police. First see these two pictures... Tanker broke down on Gujaini Highway Tanker driver Munna Prasad, a resident of Jabalpur village in Tendwari, Banda, said that he was transporting petrol after filling it from the HPCL depot in Raipur and was heading towards Shivrajpur. Meanwhile, the tanker broke down on the Gujaini elevated bridge. He had parked the tanker on the side and was trying to get it repaired by calling a mechanic. During this time, a vehicle coming from behind hit the tanker from the side and passed, damaging its side portion and causing petrol to leak. The driver first tried to stop the leakage, but could not succeed. He then asked nearby people for buckets, saying petrol was leaking from his tanker. Hearing this, people present there rushed with whatever containers they had to collect the petrol. Seeing the crowd, he immediately informed the company and the police, following which the police reached the spot shortly and brought the situation under control. Govind Nagar Inspector Rakesh Kumar Singh said that in the presence of the police, fire brigade and HPCL officials, the petrol was being transferred into another tanker.

stories.title: Modi inaugurates Noida Int'l Airport:PM says it will benefit small traders, farmers; airports rose from 74 in 2014 to 160 now
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated Phase-1 of Noida International Airport in Jewar, UP, at 12:30 pm on Saturday. Currently, it is India’s largest airport and the second-largest in Asia. Once all four phases are completed, it will become the largest airport in Asia. During the public address, PM Modi appealed to people to face the crisis arising from the Israel–US–Iran conflict in unity. He said that discussions were held yesterday with the Chief Ministers of all states, which were productive. “I urge the citizens of the country to confront this crisis calmly, patiently, and in unity. This is a crisis affecting the entire world,” he said. PM Modi says; “I earnestly appeal to all political parties to refrain from making statements during this crisis that could harm the nation. The people will never forgive actions that damage the country.” Phase-1 covers 3,300 acres, including the terminal and a runway. With one runway, the terminal will have an annual capacity to handle 3 crore passengers. The project cost is estimated at around ₹11,000 crore. : First look of Asia's largest Noida Airport The full Noida International Airport is planned over 52 sq km. Currently, China’s Beijing Daxing International Airport is the largest in Asia, covering 47 sq km. Although the complete project is scheduled for 2040, officials associated with the Noida Airport Authority said flights could begin from May. A key feature of the airport is that passengers can reach the boarding gate in under 20 minutes after entry. See these pictures of the airport

stories.title: Govt finalises blueprint for ethanol stoves to replace LPG cylinders:How is it different from other fuels?
stories.summary: Due to the ongoing war between America-Israel and Iran, there is a crisis regarding LPG supply in the country. Long queues for cooking gas have been forming in 75 districts of UP for 15 days. In this situation, the central government is working on the blueprint of ethanol stoves to reduce dependence on LPG. LPG Equipment Research Center and several IITs across the country are working on giving the final touches to ethanol stoves. Union Food Secretary Sanjeev Chopra had shared this information in Delhi on March 24. Let's understand through 6 questions what an ethanol stove is. How different is it from normal kerosene-burning stoves? Read in Bhaskar Explainer... Question 1. What is an ethanol stove? Answer. This is a stove that runs on ethanol (an alcohol-based fuel) instead of kerosene. Bioethanol is made by fermenting sugarcane, corn, wheat, rice, and other starch-containing crops. Question 2. How is it different from a kerosene stove? Answer. These are quite different from normal kerosene stoves. To light a normal stove, a small amount of spirit or kerosene is poured into the tray under the burner to light it. Then pressure is created through the pump attached to the stove tank. This causes the oil to come out through a small hole in the burner. Then the stove burner starts burning with pressure. Whereas in ethanol stoves, there is an absorbent fiber under the burner. Ethanol is poured over the burner. The absorbent fiber absorbs about 1-1.5 liters of ethanol fuel. After this, the burner is lit directly. In this, the absorbent fiber itself does not burn; the ethanol keeps burning slowly. Question 3. What are the benefits of ethanol stoves? Answer. Food cooks faster on ethanol-powered stoves because of their high flame intensity. It also produces lower carbon gas emissions. Therefore, it is considered a good option from a health perspective. 'Superblue Stoves' can burn for 15 hours on one liter of ethanol. A normal kerosene stove burns for only 3 hours with the same amount of fuel. Question 4. Is ethanol really an alternative to LPG? Answer. Ethanol stoves can work as an alternative in some situations. However, it cannot completely replace LPG in the near future. Currently, a large portion of ethanol is used for blending with petrol. The large-scale availability of affordable ethanol for cooking is limited. In such cases, the cost of ethanol based on supply could be higher compared to LPG and kerosene. The LPG distribution network in urban areas is quite strong. Question 5. When will ethanol stoves be available in the market? Answer. Ethanol stoves may soon be available in the market. In some states of the country, NITI Aayog and American NGO Project 'GAIA' have together provided such stoves in villages. The Assam government had run a pilot project in rural areas in 2018 by purchasing methanol stoves from Sweden. The Odisha government has also conducted similar experiments. Nimbkar Agricultural Research Institute has run projects in rural areas of Maharashtra. The central government is also considering installing ethanol ATMs at petrol pumps. The government has already installed such machines in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttar Pradesh, New Delhi, and Tamil Nadu in 2024. However, these machines were installed to provide ethanol fuel for vehicles. Question 6. What is the government doing to increase ethanol production? Answer. Union Food Secretary Sanjeev Chopra said on March 24 that the government is considering reducing the share of broken rice in food grains distributed through the Public Distribution System (PDS). The share of broken rice in PDS may be reduced from 25% to 10%. The government may take this decision in the next cabinet meeting. After this change, about 90 lakh tons of broken rice will be available for ethanol production every year.

stories.title: Hail hits Raebareli-Sultanpur; rain alert issued for 39 districts:Rain hits Prayagraj-Kashi at night; pole falls on car during storm in Pratapgarh
stories.summary: The spell of unseasonal rain continues in UP. Hail fell late Friday night in Sultanpur. It also rained in Prayagraj and Varanasi. In Pratapgarh, it rained with storms. In the Sadar Kotwali area, a unipole along the Ayodhya-Prayagraj highway was uprooted and fell on a parked car. Fortunately, no one was present in the car at that time. The rear part of the car was damaged. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert in 39 districts today. During this period, winds may blow at a speed of 30 km/h. According to the Meteorological Department, the weather has changed due to the effect of a Western Disturbance. It will rain with thunder and lightning for the next 4 days. Lightning may strike in some places. There is also a possibility of hail with storms. In the last 24 hours, it rained in 10 districts, including Lucknow, Kanpur, and Sitapur. In Hardoi, a farmer died due to a lightning strike. However, the average temperature in the state recorded an increase of up to 5 °C. Banda remained the hottest, where the maximum temperature was recorded at 40.2 °C. The lowest temperature was recorded in Muzaffarnagar at 15.4 °C. Lucknow's meteorologist, Atul Singh, said- Due to winds coming from Pakistan, the weather in UP has changed. A new spell of rain has begun. Another disturbance will become active on March 29. This will bring good rainfall across the state. Winds will blow at speeds of 40-50 km per hour. Temperature will drop by up to 3C. See the weather pictures- How will the weather be for the next 4 days? Storm damages wheat and pigeon pea crops. How to protect? Agricultural experts say that rain and strong winds will affect Rabi, Zaid, and horticultural crops. Currently, pods are forming in pigeon pea, mustard, chickpea, peas, mung bean, and groundnut. The grains are filling. Strong winds can cause pods to split and grains to fall off. The wheat crop can also fall due to strong winds, which risks reducing yield. In vegetables, flowers, and small fruits of okra, tomato, bottle gourd, cucumber, watermelon, muskmelon, eggplant, and chili can fall. Farmers are advised to immediately harvest crops that are ripe and store them in a safe place. Do not let water accumulate in the fields; arrange proper drainage for this. Govt says, ‘farmers can claim insurance if crops fall’ There is relief news for farmers whose crops have been damaged during recent rains and hailstorms, and amid upcoming alerts. According to the government, if crops are damaged within 14 days of harvesting, farmers can claim insurance under the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana. The district administration will survey crop damage from natural disasters and submit a report, based on which the UP government can decide to provide compensation.

stories.title: How did a shrine emerge at Nishadraj fort in Shringverpur?:Nishad Party holds protest; Muslims say it's their govt, let them build what they want
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has developed Nishadraj Park across 40 bighas in Shringverpur, Prayagraj, at a cost of around ₹37 crore. The park was inaugurated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and has since attracted large number of visitors. However, a controversy has now emerged over a shrine and a mosque located along the park’s boundary. Last week, Nishad Party chief Sanjay Nishad blocked a highway and warned that if the administration does not act, his supporters would remove the structure themselves and throw it into the Ganga. Given the sensitive religious nature of the issue, authorities are proceeding with caution. Around 20 Muslim families living near the mosque say that while the park has been built recently, the mosque has existed there for many years. The situation has raised questions over the actual timeline and ownership of the site. On what basis is Sanjay Nishad claiming this shrine-mosque is illegal? What does history say? Dainik Bhaskar's team reached the ground and looked at every aspect. Let's learn everything from one perspective... Nishadraj Park's path goes through Muslim settlement There are about 20 Muslim houses before reaching the Nishadraj Park in Shringverpur. The path leading to the park has a graveyard right next to it. There is no dispute about these. However, there is a shrine and a mosque on about 2 bighas of land right behind the park. This is the subject of dispute. On March 23, people from the Nishad community blocked National Highway-30 over this issue. Hundreds of police personnel and PAC were quickly deployed to protect the shrine. The administration somehow managed to control the situation. People were pacified with assurances of further action. Know the Questions of Hindus If the mosque is old, then how are there Lakhauri bricks underneath We met temple priest Bhagwati Prasad Mishra at Shringverpur Ghat. Bhagwati Prasad says, ‘There was discussion about removing the shrine earlier, but when Nishadraj Park was built, this discussion intensified’. Where the shrine is, right next to it is the Satya Sai Ashram. There is a minaret inside it. When the foundation was dug, Lakhauri bricks were found. The Archaeological Department also excavated here; Lakhauri bricks were found everywhere. When you look from the riverside, you will see houses made of similar bricks. Now, when there are bricks all around, then how did the shrine come up? There can't even be a question of a shrine being there. Bhagwati Prasad says, ‘This Muslim village was not here before. Gradually, people kept settling and then moved towards the Ganga. Now these people have created a boundary around the mazar. They started organizing fairs there, started having qawwali performances’. This did not happen 15-20 years ago. If everything from Raj Ghat to Ram Ghat is connected to Ram and Nishadraj, then the mazar must have been built later. People come to the shrine for various purposes Sanjay Tripathi, who was born in Shringverpur, says, ‘I have seen a lot of changes here in 15-20 years. This is the city of Nishadraj. Its history is seen in the Ramayana. There is a Satya Sai Ashram next to the shrine. 1-2 priests have even been murdered there. People go near the shrine for various purposes, both good and bad. We want the administration to resolve this issue. Because we have seen the disputes of Ayodhya, Mathura, and Kashi’. 70-year-old Kallu Ram Mishra calls this shrine site a Hanuman temple. He says that when the Muslim population increased, these people built a dome here. No one protested then. Since Nishad Party's Sanjay Nishad started coming, the opposition began. It would be good if this gets resolved. Ram Lalla had come here and bathed. Ram Lalla crossed from here. Now, if it becomes a shrine, it won't be right. Nirmal Baba of Shringverpur says, ‘I have been seeing for 20-25 years that there is a mosque there. These people organize qawwali’. Sanjay Nishad says that 3 kilometer area should be vacated, this is Nishadraj's capital. If Sanjay Nishad is saying that the mosque should be removed, then his people will remove it too. On March 23, the Nishad people had gathered in very large numbers. Now the Muslim side's perspective The shrine is always open; whoever wants to come can visit We reached the shrine from the edge of the park. It's about 2 bighas in area. There are two shrines at the beginning. Moving forward, we saw a shrine inside. Prayers are held here during Eid al-Adha. This shrine is maintained by Nankau from the village. Inside the mosque, he was sitting in front of the shrine, reading religious books. Nankau doesn't speak on camera. He says, ‘This shrine has been here for a very long time. The park was built recently. Not only Muslims but Hindus also come here’. We said that Sanjay Nishad is calling this an encroachment and blocking the highway to get it removed. Nankau says, if they want to take it, they will take it. Who can stop them? Otherwise, people have been coming here for a very long time. No one has ever faced any problem. The gate here always remains open. Whoever wants to worship comes here. The park's road went through the graveyard, and we didn't say anything In the village, we met Moharram Ali. He is retired from government service. Moharram Ali says it's their wish if they want to create disputes. Otherwise, there is no kind of conflict here. Indira Gandhi came here once. At that time, she had announced the shrine of Manari Shah Baba. Both Hindus and Muslims had garlanded her then. As far as the park is concerned, it was built just last year. The village council's 12 bighas of grazing land also went into it. Their road, which was also built, goes through the graveyard. We never raised any objection. Moharram Ali says, 'We don't want any kind of dispute. If these people want to remove it, let them tell us what harm it has caused. Have Muslims caused them any damage? Have we caused any damage to their park? You won't find anyone'. When the palanquin was lifted here, Muslims would help carry it. When some people objected, Muslims stopped carrying it, but even today, they walk alongside the palanquin. The people who were creating a ruckus with Sanjay Nishad that day were all outsiders. There is no dispute of any kind here. Now the question is, how to prove what should be here? For this, we need to look at old research... Archaeological Department conducted excavation here for 9 years The Archaeological Department conducted excavations in Shringverpur from 1977 to 1986. These excavations were carried out under the supervision of the then ASI Director General, BB Lal, and KN Dikshit. This project was named 'Archaeology of the Ramayana Sites'. About 400 meters away from where the mosque is located, a 250-meter-long permanent pond was found. It had water management and filtration systems. It was said to be about 2100 years old. Clay statues were found with religious figures carved on them. An ancient head of Shiva's statue was found. It was from the 1st-2nd century CE. 13 coins were discovered. These coins were silver currencies of King Govind Chandra of the Gaharwar dynasty of Kannauj. The brick structures that were found were identified as temple remains. Some sources also claimed that these are remains of temples associated with Sage Shringi. The excavation revealed continuity from the Gupta period to the medieval period. It is also connected to the Ramayana period. In the excavation or survey conducted by the Archaeological Department, no tomb-mosque or Islamic structure was found anywhere. Alexander Cunningham also surveyed here in the 19th century, but did not mention any tomb or Islamic structure anywhere. He mentioned remains connected to the Ramayana. Between 1950-60, the Indian Archaeology Review Reports also identified Shringverpur only in the context of Ramayana, with no mention of any tomb or mosque.

stories.title: Was Mukhtar Ansari poisoned?:Two years on, Barrack No. 16 sealed; inquiry cites heart attack, family alleges conspiracy
stories.summary: ‘I fear for my life in Banda jail. My veins ache, my limbs have gone cold. The staff are administering slow poison through food. It feels as though death could come at any moment.’ This was the final petition filed by mafia figure and former MLA Mukhtar Ansari in UP’s Barabanki Civil Court. The petition reached the court on 21 March 2024; Mukhtar died on 28 March while lodged in Banda jail. Two years on, his family continues to pursue the case. Their lawyer, Randhir Singh Suman, alleges a conspiracy by jail staff to kill Mukhtar, citing pre-death photographs, court statements and documents as evidence. He is preparing to move the Supreme Court, terming the magisterial inquiry “fabricated”. The 172-day investigation concluded that a heart attack caused Mukhtar’s death. Owing to legal procedures, everything from his clothes to his barrack remains sealed. His elder brother and Samajwadi Party MP from Ghazipur, Afzal Ansari, also alleges collusion between the government and the jail administration. Point 1: Mukhtar’s death – Natural death or planned murder On 29 March 2024, a day after Mukhtar’s death, the UP government ordered a magisterial inquiry. The investigation team included Banda DM Durga Shakti Nagpal and SP Ankur Agarwal, while Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Garima Singh was appointed as the investigating officer. The team conducted its probe over five months. The report, submitted on 16 September 2024, concluded that Mukhtar died of a heart attack, specifically a myocardial infarction. Three key points emerged from the investigation report: Mukhtar’s side counters: Lawyer Randhir Suman offers two arguments challenging these findings. First: Mukhtar’s health had been deteriorating for two weeks before his death. During a court appearance on 20 March, he alleged for the first time that he had been poisoned through food on the night of 19 March. Second: Seven days before his death, on 21 March, Mukhtar filed a petition in Barabanki Civil Court claiming he had been given slow poison in his food 40 days earlier. The food, he said, was prepared by Banda jail staff. He alleged that both staff and he consumed it, after which several employees, along with Mukhtar, fell ill. Point 2: Mukhtar’s security in jail before death According to the magisterial inquiry, all CCTV footage of the jail was examined. The report provides minute-by-minute details of how Mukhtar fell unconscious in his barrack on the evening of 28 March 2024. It states that the jail administration did not delay during the ‘golden hour’, ensuring he was transported promptly from the jail to hospital. Mukhtar’s side counter On 16 August 2021, Mukhtar told the MP/MLA court in Barabanki that there was a conspiracy to kill him in Banda jail. He alleged that officials and suspicious individuals would enter after CCTV cameras were turned away. He also claimed that some prisoners were offered ₹5 crore and relief in all cases in exchange for killing him. Point 3: Mukhtar’s medical condition in Barrack No. 16 According to the investigation team, the magisterial inquiry was based not only on doctors’ medical reports but also on statements from over 100 individuals, including inmates lodged with Mukhtar, as well as viscera laboratory findings. Yellowish patches and blockages were found in his heart muscles, indicating that the death was not sudden but the result of a worsening chronic condition. Mukhtar’s side counter Mukhtar’s son, Umar Ansari, told the court that there were injury marks on his father’s body. He claimed blood was visible from the nose and ears, the eyes were swollen, and the abdomen appeared bloated. On this basis, he argued that the death did not appear to have been caused by a heart attack. Brother Afzal says – Will bring out the truth about death Ghazipur MP Afzal Ansari has raised questions, saying, ‘I had spoken to Mukhtar on the phone before his death. His health was deteriorating. He kept saying he was being poisoned in jail, which was causing his body to break down.’ Lawyer says – Magisterial inquiry is a formality, case will reopen Advocate Randhir Suman says, ‘About 10 days before his death, Mukhtar appeared in court via video conferencing, where he alleged he was being given slow poison in jail. I filed an application on 19 March seeking his security, but despite court directions, negligence by jail staff and the administration continued.’ On claims of a natural death, he adds, ‘Magisterial inquiries into custodial deaths in Uttar Pradesh are often mere formalities. When Mukhtar was alive, his barrack was checked four to five times a day, allegedly to harass him. Food and personal items were thrown out during inspections, sometimes even at 1 am. It amounted to physical harassment.’ Advocate Randhir holds the then Banda Jail Superintendent, Viresh Raj Sharma, and jail staff responsible for Mukhtar’s death. He claims that during court questioning, the superintendent gave evasive answers, suggesting facts were being concealed. We spoke over the phone with former Banda Jail Superintendent Viresh Raj Sharma, who said that as the matter is under consideration in the Supreme Court, it would not be appropriate to comment. We then contacted the current superintendent, Alok Kumar. Alok Kumar said, ‘Barrack No. 16, along with Mukhtar’s clothes, books and personal belongings, has been sealed for investigation. The family was asked to collect his belongings, but no one came. Even after two years, the barrack remains unchanged. This is part of the investigation protocol.’ Criminal lawyer says – Claims of poisoning and contract killing are weak We spoke to Supreme Court criminal lawyer Shashwat Anand to examine the claims made by Mukhtar’s counsel, Randhir Suman. 1. Was Mukhtar poisoned through his food? Mukhtar’s lawyers are relying on applications filed in court, but what matters is the action taken on those petitions. There was a nine-day gap between the poisoning allegation and his death. This is a significant gap. During this period, the defence could have requested procedures such as stomach pumping to retrieve and test contents for poison. Presenting court applications after death, without such steps, weakens the claim. 2. Was a contract given in jail to kill Mukhtar? Merely alleging a contract killing inside jail, or unauthorised movement in the barracks, is a weak argument without evidence. Mukhtar was lodged in a high-security barrack under constant monitoring by both jail authorities and police headquarters. In such conditions, a contract killing appears less plausible. 3. Injury marks on Mukhtar’s body If visible injury marks existed, the family could have sought a second post-mortem in the High Court. The court could have ordered an independent examination by doctors and police from another state, but this was not pursued. Even now, if photographic evidence exists, a fresh petition can be filed in the High Court. However, questions would remain about the delay if such evidence was available earlier. Former IPS officer says – Mukhtar’s chapter is over, death due to illness Former UP IPS officer Rajesh Kumar Pandey, who had filed a case against Mukhtar in 2016 and was involved in operations against his gang, says, ‘The case is effectively closed. No evidence of poisoning has emerged. Afzal Ansari has repeatedly alleged poisoning, but Mukhtar died due to illness.’ However, retired 1972-batch IPS officer SR Darapuri disagrees. He says, ‘If a prisoner expresses fear of being murdered days before death and then dies within a week, it suggests something is amiss. The magistrate’s inquiry, in my view, was meaningless.’ Darapuri adds that magistrates often function under pressure from the state government. Given the known stance of the Yogi government on Mukhtar, he argues that the probe should have been handed to an independent investigating agency.

stories.title: Tenant accused of killing 8-year-old girl:Dispute with landlord results in murder, body packed in container, accused killed in encounter
stories.summary: A tenant accused of killing a businessman’s eight-year-old daughter was shot dead in a police encounter in Agra early Saturday morning. When police surrounded him, he opened fire, injuring a police officer. The police retaliated, and the accused was hit. He was taken to the district hospital, where doctors declared him dead. DCP City Syed Ali Abbas said that on Friday night, police received a tip-off that the murder accused was planning to flee to Firozabad. The accused, 29-year-old Sunil, had murdered the shoe trader’s daughter on March 24 by slitting her throat and hiding her body in a container. The body was recovered around 30 hours later. He had been absconding since the crime, and the police had announced a reward of ₹25,000 for his arrest. Police investigation revealed that about 11 days before the incident, the girl’s uncle had slapped him over unpaid rent and locked his room, which enraged him. Although he later cleared the dues, he had threatened revenge. Police say he carried out the murder to settle that grudge. The girl went missing from outside her house A youth residing in Siddharth Nagar Gobar Chowki owns a shoe factory. The businessman has 2 houses in the area. In one house, he lives with his wife and 2 daughters. The factory and warehouse are on the ground floor of the house directly opposite. A room above the house has been rented out. The accused painter Sunil lived in it. The businessman had said that some children from the neighborhood came at 2 PM on Tuesday. The elder daughter went to play with them. When she wasn't seen for a long time, I thought she must have gone for tuition. When she didn't return by 4:30 in the evening, her mother became worried. Then we started searching. Called and asked the tuition teacher. They said that the daughter hadn't come today. Police formed 4 teams, scanned neighborhood CCTV footage The father said that I informed the police. We kept searching for my daughter in the surrounding area with the neighborhood people. Police scanned CCTV cameras installed in the lanes. At 2:00 PM, the daughter was seen buying a packet of chips at a shop outside the lane. Then, she was seen returning from there. Police registered a kidnapping FIR late in the evening based on my complaint. 4 teams were formed under the leadership of ACP Piyush Kant Rai. One police team was checking cameras around the house. Another team was talking to family members and questioning neighbors. Tenant went to police station to file missing report, then went missing himself Father says, ‘The third team got involved in searching houses. Police searched every house in the neighborhood, but on Tuesday, no clue of the girl was found. Meanwhile, I told the police that tenant Sunil was with us since the girl went missing'. He was also searching for the girl. He went to the police station with me to file a missing report. They said that when police started checking houses in the neighborhood, Sunil was nowhere to be found. He had locked his room and left. When I expressed my suspicion, the police opened the tenant's room lock at 8 PM on Wednesday. After searching the room, the daughter's body was found in a canister. A flour sack was kept on top. Above it was placed a red colored quilt. Crowd created ruckus for 30 mins, threw stones on road DCP City Syed Ali Abbas said that during the investigation, the girl's body was found in a small flour canister kept in the room. When police tried to take the body for a postmortem, family members and neighborhood people started protesting. However, the police took away the body, including the canister. After this, people came out on the road and blocked the Mughal bridge on Fatehabad Road. The commotion continued for about 30 minutes. The DCP pacified the family by assuring action.
