stories.title: Student dies after accidental gunshot while filming reel:Was loading bullet into pistol himself; family alleges murder
stories.summary: A 12th-grade student in Lakhimpur was fatally injured while making a reel with a pistol. During the recording, the gun suddenly discharged, and the bullet struck him in the stomach, causing him to collapse in pain. In an attempt to control the bleeding, he pressed the wound with both hands. As his condition worsened, his friends rushed him to the hospital, where he later succumbed to his injuries. The incident had taken place on 30 March, though the video of the incident surfaced on Friday. In the footage, the student can be seen loading a bullet into the pistol moments before it accidentally fires, after which he falls. Following the incident, the family lodged a complaint with the police, alleging that their son had been kidnapped and murdered. Based on their complaint, the police have registered a case against several unidentified individuals, along with two named suspects. Two youths have been taken into custody for questioning. The incident falls under the Sadar Kotwali police station area. See two photos related to the incident Anil Kumar Jha lives with his family in Suagara village. He told the police that his son, Ansh Kumar Jha (17 years old), had left home at 8 PM on March 30 with friends. Late at night, Ansh called. The son informed that he had gone to Lucknow to get treatment for a friend's mother. The next morning, he called again and said he was returning from Lucknow. On March 31, at around 2:30 PM, Ansh called again and said he was unwell. He had been admitted to Janshakti Hospital, Gola Road, Lakhimpur. As soon as the information was received, family members reached the hospital. Here, Ansh's friends Shubham Kumar and Nitin Singh alias Mikku, along with other companions, were present. The family members allege that Ansh's friends and the hospital staff did not give them the correct information. When asked, they were told that Ansh had been burned by firecrackers. Due to this, his treatment was ongoing. On the night of March 31, at around 1 AM, doctors called the family members and informed them about Ansh's deteriorating condition. They advised taking him to Lucknow. Father came to know about the bullet injury in Lucknow Father Anil Kumar Jha took his son Ansh to Ram Manohar Lohiya Hospital in Lucknow. There, an X-ray examination revealed that Ansh had a bullet in his stomach. During treatment, his condition continued to deteriorate. He died around 6 AM on April 2. Family members say that if the correct information had been received on time, Ansh's life could have been saved with better treatment. Based on the complaint, police have registered a report naming Shubham Kumar and Nitin Singh, along with several unknown persons. Allegations of kidnapping, murder, and concealing evidence Ansh's uncle, Sunil Kumar alias Sonu, has alleged that Ansh was kidnapped and murdered. Later, attempts were made to conceal evidence. He says that several other people may also be involved in this incident. He has demanded an impartial investigation and justice from the police. Had taken admission in 12th Ansh Kumar Jha's grandfather, Dev Lakhan Jha, is retired from Uttar Pradesh Police. Ansh was a student of the city's Dharmasabha Inter College. After passing class 11th, he took admission in 12th this year. The entire family, including mother Renu Jha, brother Vansh Jha, and grandmother Ratan Mala Jha, is in shock over the son's death. Police are interrogating two friends taken into custody.

stories.title: Heavy hailstorm in Kanpur-Jalaun and Lalitpur:Several trees uprooted, wall collapses, vehicles damaged due to storm; drizzle in Lucknow
stories.summary: The weather has deteriorated once again in UP. Heavy hailstorms occurred in Kanpur, Lalitpur, and Jalaun. In Kanpur, there was rain accompanied by strong winds on Saturday evening. Several trees were uprooted in Govind Nagar here. A car was completely crushed under a fallen tree. Power supply has also been affected. Weather expert Dr. S.N. Sunil Pandey from Kanpur said that the weather may remain bad until April 5. Meanwhile, in Jalaun's Madhogarh tehsil, there was heavy rain with strong winds. Heavy hailstones also fell. A sheet of hail covered the roads and fields. The standing wheat and mustard crops in the fields were destroyed. The Meteorological Department has issued an orange alert in Lucknow. In the next few hours, there is a possibility of storms, rain, and thunderstorms at speeds of 40 to 60 kilometers per hour. Light drizzle has already started. Since Saturday morning, clouds have covered 20 cities, including Meerut-Ghaziabad. Strong winds are blowing. Alert for rain and hailstorms in 35 districts today See 3 pictures of Kanpur... Drizzle in Lucknow Heavy hailstorm in Jalaun Hailstorm in Lalitpur 5 deaths in 48 hours Hailstorm occurred in Agra late Friday night. Rain occurred in Mathura and Sambhal. A tree fell due to a storm in Kasganj. A brother and sister, standing underneath to take shelter from the rain, died after being crushed. In Mathura, rain soaked 5 thousand quintals of wheat stored in 10 thousand sacks at the Kosi Kalan grain market. In Agra, 5 mud houses collapsed. Meanwhile, 5 people have died in the state due to lightning strikes in 48 hours. These include a government teacher and his wife in Varanasi, 2 people from Chitrakoot, and one person from Lalitpur. Lucknow weather scientist Atul Singh said - A new spell of unseasonal rain has started due to the western disturbance that became active from April 3 and westerly winds bringing moisture from the Arabian Sea. A new western disturbance is becoming active from April 7. Its impact will be more visible in western UP, central region and Bundelkhand. Strong winds will blow. There will be rain. Hail will fall. Temperature will drop by 5C. See pictures of yesterday's weather- Why did the weather change again? Lucknow Meteorological Department scientist Atul Kumar Singh said that the effect of the western disturbance active in southern Afghanistan and surrounding Pakistani areas has now started showing in Uttar Pradesh. Due to this, the weather has deteriorated in western UP. Heavy rain is occurring with strong winds. Now its effect will reach the central region and Bundelkhand. Strong gusty winds will blow in many areas. Now know the condition of cities What will the weather be like for 5 days? 5 died due to a lightning strike, 2 died in storm Crops damaged by unseasonal rain and strong winds Crops have suffered significant damage due to unseasonal rain and strong winds. CM Yogi had inquired about the condition of affected farmers. He had sought reports from officials. All district magistrates were instructed to remain in alert mode. He said that farmers should not face any kind of trouble. Assess crop damage and ensure compensation to farmers soon. 15,000 farmers' crops damaged in 15 days According to the UP government, in the last 15 days, crops of 15,000 farmers spread over 4,300 hectares have been damaged. So far, 10,278 farmers have received compensation.

stories.title: Lucknow blast plot accused terrorist sent on 5-day remand:Pak connection-terror network to be interrogated; 4 youth caught by ATS
stories.summary: The four accused of the terrorist module caught in Lucknow were presented in court on Saturday, from where they were sent on a 5-day police remand. UP ATS will now interrogate them about Pakistani handlers and the terrorist network. ATS commandos presented the four accused, Shakib, Vikas Gahlawat, Lokesh alias Papla Pandit, and Arbab in the special court of Lucknow in the afternoon. Their custody remand was sought, which the court accepted and handed them over to ATS for 5 days. Conspiracy to carry out blasts in several cities, including Lucknow The preliminary investigation has revealed that the accused had conducted reconnaissance of railway property, prestigious institutions, and some political figures in cities like Lucknow, Ghaziabad, and Aligarh. The ATS is now verifying all these locations and assessing the potential threat. Trial of a bigger conspiracy through small attacks Investigation agencies suspect that the accused had demonstrated a 'trial' to their handlers by first carrying out small-scale arson incidents. They also received payments by sending videos of these incidents, which further boosted their confidence. After the case was exposed, the state's security agencies have been put on alert. Surveillance has been increased at sensitive locations so that any potential threat can be prevented in time. Important clues may be found from recovered items Inflammable materials, 7 smartphones, and several objectionable pamphlets have been recovered from the arrested accused. ATS is conducting a forensic examination of these digital devices, which is likely to yield important clues related to chats, transactions, and foreign contacts. Focus on investigating connections with Pakistani handlers According to ATS officials, the biggest focus during interrogation will be to understand the network connected to the accused's Pakistani handlers. It will also be ascertained through which mediums contact was being made and which locations were being targeted.

stories.title: Lakhs of teachers protest in Delhi against TET mandatory requirement:30 thousand teachers from UP joins; demands govt to bring ordinance
stories.summary: Around 30,000 teachers from Uttar Pradesh staged a protest at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan on Saturday against the mandatory TET requirement. Teachers from nearly 20 states, including Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Karnataka, also joined in large numbers. They raised slogans like “Remove TET, save teachers” and “We won’t let our rights be taken away.” The teachers submitted a memorandum addressed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi at the PMO, demanding an ordinance against the Supreme Court’s September 1, 2025, order. They also sought a law in Parliament to exempt teachers from the mandatory TET requirement. Teachers Federation of India national president Dr Dinesh Chandra Sharma said the Supreme Court’s decision could push lakhs of families into unemployment. He warned that if the Centre does not intervene, they will gherao Parliament. In September 2025, the Supreme Court made it mandatory for all teachers up to junior high school level across the country to pass the Teacher Eligibility Test (TET). The order has put the jobs of around 1.87 lakh teachers in Uttar Pradesh at risk. Teachers put forward two more demands Teachers who fail to clear TET by September 1, 2027, should not be dismissed, but treated as retired so they can receive a pension and benefits. Teachers appointed before August 23, 2010 (before the RTE Act came into force) should be completely exempt from TET. Dr Sharma said over 20 lakh teachers across the country are at risk due to the ruling, making it essential for the government to intervene and secure their livelihoods. UP Primary Teachers’ Association general secretary Sanjay Singh said TET was implemented in the state on July 27, 2011, and imposing it on those appointed earlier is unfair. Background of the case The Supreme Court bench of Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Augustine George Masih, while hearing petitions from Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra, ruled that teachers with more than five years of service remaining must pass TET. Otherwise, they would have to resign or opt for compulsory retirement. The court also directed state governments to ensure all teachers clear the TET within two years. Several political parties, including the Samajwadi Party, raised the issue in Parliament, demanding relief through an ordinance, but the Centre declined, citing the court’s order. Following the decision, protests erupted across Uttar Pradesh. Two teachers, one in Hamirpur and another in Mahoba, reportedly died, with families claiming they were distressed after the ruling. Several states, including Uttar Pradesh, have filed review petitions, which are pending before the Supreme Court. If accepted, the original order could be stayed. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had earlier said that teachers are experienced and trained by the government, and their capability should not be overlooked. In Uttar Pradesh, about 1.86 lakh teachers appointed before July 29, 2011, have not cleared TET. Around 50,000 of them are not even eligible to appear for the exam. These include teachers appointed with minimum qualifications, such as intermediate and BTC, dependent appointments, and BPEd-qualified physical education teachers. UP TET exam in July The UP TET 2026 exam will be held on July 2, 3 and 4. Applications began on March 27, with the last date set as April 26. The fee for General and OBC candidates has been increased to ₹2,000. The last date for corrections in the application form is May 1. The exam is being conducted after nearly four years; the previous exam in November 2021 was cancelled due to a paper leak and was later held in January 2022. Teachers took to the streets against the Supreme Court's order. Protests took place in all districts of UP.

stories.title: CM Mohan Yadav visits famous Kashi shop; asks ‘what’s special:Orders kachori-sabzi, lassi; urges people to watch Vikramaditya Mahanatya play
stories.summary: Madhya Pradesh CM Mohan Yadav remained in Varanasi for the second day. On Saturday morning, he along with his wife Seema Yadav, reached the city's famous Ram Bhandar shop. He asked the shopkeeper, "What will you serve? Listening to CM Yadav, the shopkeeper smiled. The CM then ordered Kachori and Lassi as he sat and had breakfast with common people. Despite the shopkeeper denying, CM Yadav himself paid the bill. After eating, CM Yadav conversed with the media. During the conversation, he said, “Do go and watch Vikramaditya Mahanatya play.” See pictures It is my good fortune that Baba called me twice in 7 days CM Mohan Yadav said, “By the grace of Baba Vishwanath, he got the opportunity to visit Kashi twice in 7 days. This is my good fortune. There is spiritual energy in the city. The CM also praised the great play based on Vikramaditya, organized in Kashi. He said, ”This performance is truly wonderful and whoever comes to Kashi must see it." On April 3, the grand theatrical performance of Vikramotsav 2026 was inaugurated On April 3, CM Yogi and Yadav inaugurated the grand theatrical performance of Vikramotsav 2026. During the event, CM Mohan Yadav also presented a Vedic clock to Yogi. Madhya Pradesh CM Mohan Yadav said, “What Chief Minister Yogiji said is very important. The pair of 3 brothers is famous in the world. The example of what kind of relationship should exist between brothers is found in the pair of Lord Shri Krishna and Balram ji. Similarly, the pair of Bhartrihari and Maharaj Vikramaditya is equally famous.” In the tradition of Vikramaditya, Maharaja Bhartrihari became established in the Nath Sampradaya. Ujjain was the land of his initiation. The fort of Chunar, near Kashi, was the land of his spiritual practice. It is said that the construction of Chunar fort is also associated with the name of Maharaja Bhartrihari. When the proposal for the presentation of this theatrical adaptation came before the Government of Madhya Pradesh, my first suggestion was that it should be organized in Kashi. Mohan Yadav said, ‘Among the artists of the event, some are doctors, some are engineers’ Mohan Yadav said, “The trio of three brothers became famous, the third one belongs to Vikramaditya's brothers. We are becoming familiar with that period of generosity and bravery. Which is happening today in the Prime Minister's constituency. This event is strengthening the development and natural relations between the two states. Among the artists of this event, some are doctors, engineers, who are dedicated to Vikramaditya.”

stories.title: Lions Simba Sultan await their 'bride' in Etawah Safari:Year-long search for a mating partner yet to yield success
stories.summary: The search for a suitable “bride” for Etawah Safari Park’s nine-and-a-half-year-old Asiatic lions Simba and Sultan has turned into a long-running tale. For nearly one-and-a-half years, efforts have been underway, but the royal bachelors are still waiting. Now, the safari management has renewed hope by initiating steps to bring a lioness named Sudha from Rohtak Zoo in Haryana. Born to be stars, now ready to settle According to Safari Director Dr Anil Kumar Patel, Simba and Sultan were born in October 2016 to lions Manan and Jessica. Over the years, the duo has grown into the main attractions of the safari, drawing visitors with their majestic presence. Now fully grown, the focus has shifted from fame to family, with plans to expand their lineage. Why the in-house match didn’t work Interestingly, the lionesses already present in the safari are siblings of Simba and Sultan. This makes breeding within the park impossible, forcing authorities to look beyond their territory. Bringing in a new lioness has now become essential to ensure the next generation of Asiatic lions at the safari. Sudha, the likely bride-to-be The spotlight is now on Sudha, a lioness from Rohtak Zoo, who is emerging as a strong contender. Talks are progressing, and if all goes as planned, she could soon arrive in Etawah. In exchange, a male lion named Vishwa, born at the safari on World Lion Day in 2022, will be sent to Rohtak. A bride with experience matters Sudha is no stranger to motherhood, having delivered cubs twice earlier. This has raised optimism among officials that she will be able to successfully breed in Etawah as well. However, before finalising the move, her health will be thoroughly checked, with samples to be tested at IVRI Bareilly and NCBS Bengaluru. Matchmaking needs official approvals The transfer process will only be completed after approval from the Central Zoo Authority in New Delhi. Meanwhile, the safari management is also in touch with other zoos, including Sakkarbaug Zoo in Gujarat and Rajgir Zoo in Bihar, to explore more options. Past promises, present hopes About a year and a half ago, Gujarat had assured the availability of a lioness, but the plan did not materialise. Since then, the search has continued across states. Officials remain hopeful that Simba and Sultan will soon find their long-awaited companion, strengthening both their family line and the safari’s appeal.

stories.summary: UP Politics: लखनऊ में सपा के राष्ट्रीय अध्यक्ष अखिलेश यादव की अध्यक्षता में आगामी विधानसभा चुनाव की तैयारियों को लेकर एक महत्वपूर्ण बैठक हुई। इस बैठक में पार्टी के जिलाध्यक्षों और अन्य पदाधिकारियों को कई सख्त निर्देश दिए गए। अखिलेश यादव ने जिलाध्यक्षों को साफ चेतावनी दी कि वे किसी भी व्यक्ति को टिकट दिलाने का ठेका न लें। उन्होंने कहा कि अगर किसी जिलाध्यक्ष के खिलाफ ऐसी कोई शिकायत आई, तो पार्टी में उसकी खैर नहीं होगी। अखिलेश यादव ने यह भी स्पष्ट किया कि अगर कोई जिलाध्यक्ष खुद चुनाव लड़ना चाहता है, तो उसे पहले चुपचाप अपने जिलाध्यक्ष पद से इस्तीफा दे देना चाहिए। इस्तीफा देने के बाद उसे उच्च कमान को सूचित करना होगा। उसके बाद ही पार्टी इस पर विचार करेगी। उन्होंने साफ कहा कि कोई भी जिलाध्यक्ष खुद को प्रत्याशी घोषित न करे।

stories.title: Shiksha Mitras in UP to receive ₹18,000 starting this month:CM Yogi announces hike in honorarium for instructors
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath launched the ‘School Chalo Abhiyan’ from Varanasi at 10 am on Saturday. He personally placed school bags on the shoulders of children at a government school in Shivpur, distributed gifts and books, and enquired about their well-being. He later served food to the children himself. Addressing the programme, the CM attacked the Samajwadi Party government. He said that before 2017, education was not on the government’s agenda. Their people encouraged cheating so that studies would not take place in schools. Such stop-gap arrangements cannot help society progress. Adjustment of Shiksha Mitras was cancelled on July 25, 2017 The appointment of Shiksha Mitras in Uttar Pradesh began in 2001. During the Samajwadi Party government in 2013–14, they were adjusted as assistant teachers. Those who were not adjusted filed a petition in the Allahabad High Court. On September 12, 2015, the High Court ordered the cancellation of this adjustment. The state government challenged it in the Supreme Court, which, on July 25, 2017, upheld the decision and cancelled the adjustment. Reverted from assistant teachers to Shiksha Mitras Following the Supreme Court’s order, around 1.72 lakh assistant teachers were reverted to Shiksha Mitras. Their salary dropped from ₹50,000 to a monthly honorarium of ₹3,500. This led to large protests in Lucknow by Shiksha Mitras from across the state. After the protest, the government increased the honorarium from ₹3,500 to ₹10,000 per month. It also announced 68,500 assistant teacher posts, giving Shiksha Mitras priority in recruitment. They were given age relaxation and 25 bonus marks. Later, in 2019, 69,000 assistant teacher posts were announced, again with benefits for Shiksha Mitras. Over 13,000 Shiksha Mitras became assistant teachers through these recruitments. BJP government promised a solution in 2017 There are around 1.42 lakh Shiksha Mitras in state-run schools. The teacher-student ratio should ideally be 1:30, but due to their presence, it is about 1:22. Education Minister Sandeep Singh said there is currently no need for new assistant teacher recruitment. Honorarium for instructors doubled in 2017, but not implemented In 2017, instructors’ honorarium was increased from about ₹9,000 to ₹17,000, but the decision was not implemented after the change in government. Instructors moved the Lucknow bench of the High Court. A single bench ordered payment of ₹17,000 with 9% interest. The state challenged it, and a division bench allowed payment for only one year. The matter then reached the Supreme Court. On February 5, the Supreme Court dismissed the state’s appeal against the hike and ordered that instructors should not be removed from service. The court also stated that even after the contract period ends, their jobs will continue, as they have been working for over 10 years. It directed that the ₹17,000 honorarium be implemented from 2017. CM launches ‘School Chalo Abhiyan’ from Varanasi The Chief Minister launched the campaign at a government school in Shivpur, Varanasi, at 10 am. He personally gave school bags, gifts, and books to children, enquired about their well-being, and later served them food. He also criticised the previous Samajwadi Party government, saying education was not a priority before 2017 and copying in exams was encouraged, which hindered social progress. Before the event, the CM visited Kaal Bhairav temple and later offered prayers at Kashi Vishwanath temple following proper rituals. Key Points from CM’s Address 1. Over ₹80,000 crore spent on school education Yogi said that more than ₹80,000 crore is being spent on school education in Uttar Pradesh, and results must reflect this investment. Funds have been allocated in the current budget for Kasturba Gandhi schools, where they did not exist earlier. Education in these schools earlier went only up to Class 8, after which girls dropped out. The government has decided to extend this up to Class 12. 2. Dilapidated schools before 2017 He recalled that when his government came to power in 2017, the ‘School Chalo Abhiyan’ was launched on 1 July. Before that, he had visited several districts and seen the poor condition of basic education buildings. He visited a school where the principal said student numbers were declining and had dropped below 10. He was told children lacked interest in studies. The CM responded by asking whether it was the children lacking interest or the teachers lacking the will to teach. He said it is the responsibility of educators to spark curiosity among students. 3. Education key to social and economic equality Yogi said that social and economic equality can only be achieved through education. Earlier, the school dropout rate had crossed 19%, but it has now come down to 3%. The aim is to bring it down to zero. He said education is not just about degrees or certificates, but about instilling values and guiding individuals on the right path. This responsibility has been entrusted to teachers, and if fulfilled properly, it will benefit both society and the nation. 4. 1.36 lakh schools upgraded with facilities He said ‘Operation Kayakalp’ has achieved new heights, and even NITI Aayog has recognised it as a success story in education. Under this initiative, over 1.36 lakh schools have been equipped with facilities. Through ‘Operation Nipun’, children’s curiosity towards learning has increased. He cited an example of a school he revisited after three years, where student strength had grown to over 250, and the principal was selected for the President’s Award. 5. Earlier, over 60% girls walked barefoot The CM said that before 2017, more than 60% of girls walked barefoot and had only one worn-out dress, irrespective of weather conditions. Boys were in a similar situation. He said that now, under the “double engine” government, all children in basic education receive two sets of uniforms, school bags, books, shoes, and socks free of cost. Funds will be transferred to parents’ accounts in two phases after the admission process begins post 15 April and 15 July. 6. ‘I still touch my teachers’ feet’ Yogi told teachers that they have been entrusted with shaping the nation’s future. If they fulfil this responsibility honestly, they will be respected throughout their lives. He said he still touches the feet of his teachers whenever he meets them, out of respect. He emphasised that teachers not only provided education but also introduced him to knowledge, which is why he continues to honour them. He added that such values must be instilled in children. He also mentioned that two CM Composite Schools have been established in every district in the first phase, and provisions have been made in the budget for two more, so that children can receive modern education from pre-primary to Class 10–12 within a single campus.

stories.title: First photo of burqa-clad robbery accused surfaces:Woman planned to flee from Ayodhya with beau after jewellery heist
stories.summary: The first photograph of the accused Burqa-clad woman who carried out a jewellery robbery in Ayodhya has surfaced. The accused, identified as Payal (25), belongs to the Hindu community. The image retrieved from the accused female's Instagram account indicates she was active in creating short videos (reels). She had uploaded seven videos in the past week, including one featuring her boyfriend Rahul (27). Planned robbery with lover Police revealed that Payal and Rahul had conspired to commit the robbery about a week in advance. They reportedly surveyed the market for three days before executing the crime on April 2 at around 12:30 pm. To conceal her identity, Payal borrowed a burqa from a friend. During the robbery, Rahul waited nearby on a motorcycle while Payal entered the jewellery shop. She used a toy pistol to threaten the shop owner and fled with gold ornaments worth approximately ₹3.6 lakh, including a necklace and chain. She later escaped on the motorcycle with Rahul. The duo was planning to flee from Ayodhya but was apprehended before they could do so. Arrest and police action While presenting the case, the police brought Rahul to the press conference, whereas Payal was directly sent to jail after being produced in court. The stolen jewellery and the fake pistol used in the crime have been recovered. Police formed five teams and examined footage from around 60 CCTV cameras. The motorcycle’s registration number helped trace the suspects. Rahul was first arrested, and based on his interrogation, Payal was later apprehended from a nearby village. 2 pictures of accused Payal How the robbery unfolded On April 2, Payal entered Mahesh Jewellers in the Kothi market area under Rudauli police station limits. Pretending to be a customer, she asked to see a gold necklace and chain. She requested water and snacks, sending the shop staff out briefly. As the shopkeeper attended to other work, Payal picked up the jewellery and attempted to leave. When confronted, she pulled out a pistol from her waist and threatened to shoot if stopped. She then fled the shop and escaped with Rahul waiting nearby. Family reacts: “Stubborn since childhood” Payal’s family expressed shock over the incident. Her sister described her as stubborn and headstrong, saying she rarely listened to anyone in the family. Her father, Ram Naval, said she had left home claiming she was going to get a Talisman made due to frequent illness. “We don’t know why she did this,” he added. Personal background Payal got married on April 5 last year and is currently four months pregnant. She had been living in Punjab with her husband and had returned to her parental home in Ayodhya to appear for her intermediate exams. Her father runs a vehicle washing center, and the shop is named after Payal. The family owns property in multiple locations. She is the third among four sisters. Rahul, on the other hand, is unemployed and lives separately with his mother. His father has passed away, and his brothers work in different places. Security concerns raised The robbery occurred about 45 km from the Ram Temple, raising concerns over law and order in the region. According to Rural SP Balwant Chaudhary, the crime was premeditated and executed with planning. He stated that the accused were arrested using CCTV footage and technical evidence, and further investigation is ongoing.

stories.title: 1671 drivers in UP draw salary without driving buses:Corporation's report also finds 1069 conductors in 'zero km' category
stories.summary: The latest review report of the Uttar Pradesh Transport Corporation has raised serious questions over the department’s functioning. Between January 2025 and February 2026, as many as 1671 drivers across the state were found to have not driven a single kilometre, yet continued to receive salaries. Alongside this, 1069 conductors were also recorded in the ‘zero km’ category. This figure points not just to negligence, but a larger failure of the monitoring system. On one hand, there have been repeated claims of staff shortage in bus operations, while on the other, thousands of employees are not working at all. Impact on bus operations, passengers face inconvenience The review clearly shows that in several regions, shortage of drivers and conductors has affected bus services. Many routes are witnessing delays or reduced services due to lack of operational staff. In contrast, a large number of drivers and conductors have been deployed in office work, staff car duties and other non-transport assignments, creating imbalance in the system. This is directly impacting passengers. Rising ‘zero km’ numbers, figures reach nearly half of drivers According to the report, the percentage of ‘zero kilometre’ drivers has reached 50%, while among conductors it stands at 34%. Such a large number of regular staff staying away from bus operations is not only causing financial loss to the corporation, but also affecting its service reliability. Earlier orders ineffective, poor implementation on ground The headquarters had earlier issued instructions that regular and capable drivers and conductors must be deployed strictly in bus operations. However, these orders were not implemented effectively at the ground level. In many places, staff were completely diverted to other duties, weakening the operational system. No work beyond bus operations now Taking the matter seriously, the transport corporation headquarters has now issued clear directions to all regional managers that drivers and conductors should not be assigned any work other than bus operations. It has also been ordered that the practice of using them in office or support roles must stop immediately, with priority given to bus services. List of names sought, action likely The headquarters has sought a detailed list of drivers and conductors who remained at ‘zero km’ between September 2025 and February 2026. This indicates that the matter will not remain limited to review, and accountability will be fixed with possible action. The role of officials may also come under scrutiny.

stories.title: Major reshuffle planned in UP BJP:Leaders lobby in Delhi for Pankaj Chaudhary's team; several faces to be dropped
stories.summary: UP BJP is preparing for major changes in its team. The party is preparing to remove long-standing leaders to develop new leadership. The ruling party is also planning to find new alternatives for leaders who reached Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council while being state office bearers. By April 30, many new faces are expected to be seen in State President Pankaj Chaudhary's team. This is why many leaders are running to Delhi to secure a place in the team. Know how many members are there in state president's organizational team New members are elected every 3 years The current organizational team of UP BJP was formed by Bhupendra Chaudhary on March 25, 2023. At that time, he was the state president. The rules in the party are such that members should be elected every 3 years. Therefore, state president Pankaj Chaudhary is working from the scratch to form a new team. Most importantly, this is an election year. Due to the Assembly-2027 elections, balancing caste and regional equations in the state team is no less than a challenge. Advice sought from CM to former office bearers In this regard, advice has been sought from CM Yogi, Deputy CMs Keshav Prasad Maurya, Brajesh Pathak, and General Secretary (Organization) Dharampal Singh for forming the state team. To ensure no equation is missed, discussions are also being held with office bearers of RSS's Western and Eastern provinces. Not only this, the state president is also taking advice from former state presidents and former office bearers of the party. He believes that such workers should be included in the state team who can handle election management, booth management and coordination with workers during the assembly elections. Will learn lessons from district committees A BJP office bearer said, “In recent days, district and municipal committees were formed. In this, questions were raised at various places about BJP's decisions. It was also observed that people working against the party line and involved in criminal activities were also given importance in the organization. Learning from this, such faces will not be given place in the state team that would raise questions on the party's credibility”. 2 suggestions to adjust BJP office bearers Two opinions of core committee office bearers have emerged in forming the state team- Leaders making recommendations up to Delhi for positions Officials saying, if we are changed there will be losses Regarding this change, current BJP officials have started putting pressure on the state leadership. State general secretaries, state vice presidents, and state ministers are contacting BJP and Sangh officials from Lucknow to Delhi to save their positions. They argue that due to having years of experience, they have deep knowledge from the mandal to the regional level. If they are removed, the party could suffer losses in the election year. Even if a new face is given a chance from the caste they belong to, the party will not benefit as much. Tug-of-war for positions in the organization is inevitable, because there are many benefits Why is there so much tug-of-war over positions in the state organization? This can be understood as the Assembly elections 2027 are near. Panchayat elections are also to be held. State office bearers play an important role in the selection of candidates in these. Office bearers get long-term political benefits by getting tickets for their close workers. Not only this, becoming state vice president or general secretary also clears the path to Legislative Council or Rajya Sabha. That's why two types of efforts are visible at this time. First- Current state office bearers are trying to save their positions. Second- New faces are putting in full effort to get positions. Now Know the Entire UP Team of BJP State President State General Secretary Organization State General Secretary State Vice President State Ministers Treasurer Co-Treasurer New Regional Presidents Will Be Seen in the Party BJP has divided UP into 6 organizational regions. Awadh, Kanpur, Gorakhpur, Kashi, Braj and West. A regional team has also been formed in each region. All 6 presidents may be changed. New faces in the party will get a chance in their place. Current regional presidents can be adjusted in front line positions.

stories.title: OT technician removed MBA student’s kidney:Performed illegal transplant in Kanpur; probe reveals accused’s role
stories.summary: In a shocking development in the Kanpur kidney racket, police are searching for Delhi-based accused Mudassar Ali Siddiqui, who allegedly removed a kidney from an MBA student and transplanted it into a woman. Investigations have revealed that Siddiqui is not a qualified doctor or urologist, as he claimed, but an Operation Theatre (OT) technician. Despite this, he allegedly carried out the kidney transplant procedure. How was the OT technician performing kidney transplants? How big is his role in the kidney scandal...? In how many states did he travel by flight to perform kidney transplants? Such questions are now arising in the minds of officials. Read the report… Accused on the run, identity exposed After interrogating an OT technician arrested on April 2, a police team reached Uttam Nagar in Delhi to trace Siddiqui. However, he was found absconding. During questioning, his family disclosed that Siddiqui works as OT staff in a hospital and is not a certified urologist. So far, eight people have been arrested in connection with the case. Key questions in investigation Officials are now probing several critical aspects of the case: The investigation is being led by DCP West, IPS officer S.M. Qasim Abidi. Two OT technicians, Kuldeep Singh Raghav and Rajesh Kumar, were sent to jail after questioning. They revealed that Siddiqui had traveled with them by flight from Delhi to Kanpur. He allegedly performed the surgery—removing the kidney from donor Ayush and transplanting it into recipient Parul Tomar. Both patients were later shifted to separate hospitals. Previous transplant linked to accused Police said Siddiqui had also conducted a kidney transplant about four months ago, in December, at Medilife Hospital in Kalyanpur’s Maswanpur area in Kanpur. When police visited the hospital, they found it shut. The owner has reportedly gone underground since the scam surfaced. Hospital partners absconding Investigations revealed that Medilife Hospital is run in partnership by three doctors—Dr. Rohan (from Tirva, Kannauj), Dr. Sandeep (from Saurikh, Kannauj), and Dr. Narendra (from Auraiya). All three have been missing since the scam came to light. Their Kanpur residences and native places have been found locked. Police suspect their involvement in the illegal transplant operations. Links to Meerut doctors emerge The probe has also uncovered links to three doctors from Meerut—Anurag alias Amit, Dr. Vaibhav Mudgal, and Dr. Afzal. Dr. Amit is reportedly a partner at Alpha Hospital in Meerut, while Dr. Mudgal is a dentist. They are suspected of arranging donors and recipients for illegal kidney transplants. All three have been absconding since the case was exposed. Their clinics are shut, and their mobile phones are switched off. Police intensify search operations Police teams are conducting raids based on inputs from Kanpur and Meerut to trace all absconding accused. Authorities say more arrests are likely as the investigation progresses. The case has exposed a deeply concerning network involved in illegal organ transplants, raising serious questions about oversight in medical procedures.

stories.title: Can Dalit voters be game-changers in 2027 UP polls?:SP banks on Constitution; Congress leans on Jagjivan Ram's legacy
stories.summary: Two recent political statements have made it clear that Dalit voters—who constitute around 21% of Uttar Pradesh’s population—could play a decisive role in the 2027 Assembly elections. “Mayawati only used Dalits and later abandoned them. Even today, Dalits and weaker sections remain marginalized,” said Ajay Rai on April 2. “We will celebrate Ambedkar Jayanti at the village level and discuss the threats facing the Constitution,” said Akhilesh Yadav on April 3. These remarks indicate that both the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Congress are actively trying to consolidate Dalit voters ahead of the elections. Congress revives Jagjivan Ram’s legacy Jagjivan Ram, India’s first Dalit Deputy Prime Minister, played a crucial role in the 1971 India-Pakistan war that led to the creation of Bangladesh. As Agriculture Minister, he also contributed to the Green Revolution. His rise to the top echelons of power sent a strong message that Dalits could play a decisive role in mainstream politics. Although Jagjivan Ram hailed from Bihar, Congress used his legacy for decades to maintain a strong hold over Dalit voters in Uttar Pradesh. Read in this report… Congress outreach through Meira Kumar To reinforce this connection, Congress is organizing a seminar in Lucknow on the eve of Jagjivan Ram’s birth anniversary (April 4). The party has invited his daughter Meira Kumar and Dalit thinker and Delhi University professor Ratan Lal as key speakers. Through this, Congress aims to send a message that Dalit interests are best protected under its leadership. Party workers have also been instructed to spend more time in Dalit localities and engage directly with their concerns. Why Dalit votes matter Senior journalist Ratan Mani Lal explains that Dalits constitute around 20–21% of UP’s population. There are 84 Assembly seats reserved for Scheduled Castes, and nearly 120 constituencies where Dalit voters exceed one lakh. Since Mayawati weakened after 2012, there has been no single dominant Dalit leader to unify the community. In 2014, a significant section of Dalit voters supported Narendra Modi, contributing to the BJP’s sweeping victories. However, voting trends suggest that such support typically lasts about a decade before voters begin exploring alternatives. Dalit vote shifts and Political competition After a BSP rally on October 9, 2025, there were indications that Dalit voters were returning to Mayawati. This prompted SP and Congress to intensify efforts to prevent a consolidation of Dalit votes in BSP’s favor. Their strategy showed partial success in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, where the alliance secured around 43% of the vote in UP, with significant support from Dalit voters. They now aim to replicate this in the 2027 Assembly polls. Election data reflects changing trends In the 2022 Assembly elections, Congress contested 399 seats independently but won only two, with a vote share of 2.33%. However, in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, the party won six seats and increased its vote share to 9.46%. The Samajwadi Party also saw a 2% increase in vote share compared to 2022. Percentage of Major Dalit Sub-Castes Search for a new Dalit leadership Senior journalist Sharat Pradhan notes that Dalits once saw Jagjivan Ram’s image reflected in Mayawati. However, as her influence declined post-2012, dissatisfaction grew among Dalit voters. This has led to the emergence of new leaders like Chandrashekhar Azad. Congress, traditionally seen as the “old home” of Dalits, regained some traction in 2024, aided by Rahul Gandhi’s campaign centered on the narrative that the Constitution is under threat. This messaging also benefited SP, helping consolidate Dalit support for the opposition alliance. Dalit sub-castes and Voting patterns Dalits make up about 20.7% of UP’s population (around 41.4 million people) and are divided into 66 sub-castes. Six major sub-castes account for 87% of the Dalit population The remaining 60 sub-castes are smaller and fragmented Among them, the Jatav community is the most influential and forms the core vote base of BSP. Non-Jatav Dalits—including Pasi, Kori, Dhobi, Khatik, and Balmiki communities—are more divided. The BJP successfully consolidated these groups between 2017 and 2024. However, in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, a section of non-Jatav voters shifted towards the opposition alliance, contributing to its strong performance with 43 seats.

stories.title: Muslim cleric held for abusing CM Yogi’s mother:Detained from his hometown in Bihar after video surfaces on social media
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (STF) has arrested Maulana Abdul Salim Chaturvedi for allegedly making inflammatory remarks against the mother of Yogi Adityanath. The cleric, a resident of Jokihat in Araria district, Bihar, was detained from his hometown by the STF. AIMIM MLA confirms arrest, initial confusion over custody Akhtarul Iman confirmed the arrest on Monday, stating that the Maulana was picked up from his assembly constituency. He initially expressed uncertainty over whether it was a case of abduction or official detention, saying local information suggested that unidentified individuals had taken the cleric away. However, after contacting officials, it was clarified that the STF had taken him into custody following due legal procedure. Case registered after controversial remarks The controversy stems from remarks allegedly made by the Maulana during a religious gathering in Bihar in the month of Ramadan. A video of the speech surfaced on social media, triggering outrage. Following the incident, Hindu organizations and members of the BJP demanded action. A case was subsequently registered against him in Balrampur, Uttar Pradesh. Bihar Police initially unaware According to Akhtarul Iman, local police authorities in Bihar initially said they had no information about the development. Later, STF officials confirmed that the arrest was carried out lawfully and the cleric was being taken for further legal action. Maulana claims video was forged In response to the allegations, Maulana Abdul Salim released a video statement claiming that his remarks had been selectively edited and taken out of context. He alleged that the viral clip misrepresented his speech and was circulated to malign his image. His supporters have called for an impartial investigation into the matter.

stories.title: Sitapur mosque razed after court order:Pre-dawn bulldozer action on illegal structure built on pond land
stories.summary: A mosque in Sitapur was demolished in the early hours of Monday after authorities carried out a bulldozer action following a court order. The structure, built around 12 years ago, was razed between 3 AM and 8 AM in the presence of senior officials and heavy police deployment. Additional District Magistrate Nitish Kumar reached the site with officials during the night, after which bulldozers were deployed to carry out the demolition. Mosque built on alleged pond land The mosque, located in Nayagaon Behti village under Laharpur Kotwali area, about 42 km from the district headquarters, was reportedly constructed on land classified as a pond and cemetery. Officials said the demolition followed a complaint by the Gram Sabha, which claimed the structure was an illegal encroachment on public land. 3 pictures of bulldozer action... Court order and notice period The Tehsil Court had ordered the demolition after hearing the case. On 6 January 2026, the court declared the mosque illegal and directed eviction. A notice period was given to remove essential items, but authorities said the structure was not cleared within the stipulated time. The administration had earlier issued a notice under Section 67 of the Uttar Pradesh Revenue Code, which allows eviction from unauthorized occupation of government or Gram Panchayat land. Heavy security deployed A large security presence was deployed during the operation to maintain law and order. Senior officers, including ASP Alok Singh and SDM Akanksha Gautam, were present at the site. Police deployment included multiple platoons, station heads from several police stations, sub-inspectors, and hundreds of constables. Mosque details and dispute The mosque, named ‘Syed Hazrat Umar Farooq’, was constructed on approximately 0.243 hectares of land. It included a large hall and four smaller rooms. According to local claims, the land is valued at around ₹6 crore, while construction cost was estimated at ₹1 crore. The dispute over the land had been ongoing for some time, with the Gram Sabha maintaining that the mosque was built on land reserved for a pond and cemetery. Religious leader calls it political issue Maulana Abdul Rahman, associated with the mosque, declined to comment on the demolition, stating that it was a political matter and it would not be appropriate for him to speak on it. ADM explained reason for night action ADM Nitish Kumar says- Due to being on the side of the main road, the operation was started at night so that traffic would not be disrupted and no one would face any difficulties. The action is being taken completely under the law. Removing encroachment from government land is the administration's priority. Currently, the situation in the area is reported to be under control. The administration is maintaining continuous surveillance.

Officer Diksha Sharma has been transferred from Hamirpur to Lucknow. New IG appointment after retirement Following the retirement of Rajesh Saxena, Chandra Prakash has been appointed as Inspector General (IG) at the Security Headquarters. He was previously posted in the Training Directorate. Shahjahanpur SP removed after controversy In Shahjahanpur, SP Rajesh Dwivedi has been removed following a recent controversy over the vandalism of martyrs’ statues. The incident had drawn criticism from opposition parties, after which police registered an FIR. Bahraich SP shifted after complaints Bahraich SP Ram Nayan Singh has been shifted after complaints regarding his working style. Public representatives had recently met Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, alleging that the officer was not responding to their calls. Following this, Singh has been transferred to the 49th Battalion PAC in Noida.

stories.title: 28 lakh UP students receives 3,350 crore scholarship:13.52 lakh OBC students benefit; CM Yogi claims, 'SP earlier used to take half the funds'
stories.summary: Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath transferred scholarships worth ₹3,350 crore to the bank accounts of 28 lakh students on Monday. Additionally, assistance of ₹100 crore was also provided to dependent members of 33,334 poor families under the National Family Benefit Scheme. CM Yogi said, we wanted to give scholarships from day one, but there were many flaws. In the SP government, SC-ST children were not given scholarships. Scholarship money was diverted to other works. When our government came to power in 2017, we had to give scholarships from SP's tenure as well. Today all students are receiving scholarships on time. More than 28 lakh students get relief At Jupiter Hall of Indira Gandhi Pratishthan in Lucknow, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directly transferred scholarship and fee reimbursement amount of ₹3,350 crore to the bank accounts of 27,99,982 students from underprivileged and weaker sections studying in classes 9 and 10 as well as post-secondary level. This amount has been transferred directly to the beneficiaries' accounts through DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer). Poor families also get support On this occasion, the Chief Minister also transferred ₹100 crore to the accounts of 33,334 dependent beneficiaries under the National Family Benefit Scheme. This amount was given to provide financial support to dependent members of poor families after the death of their main earning member. Yogi govt's focus on weaker sections Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said that the government's effort is to ensure that no eligible student drops out of studies due to financial constraints. Transparency has increased by sending scholarships directly to accounts through DBT and students are getting timely help.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:CM hikes Anganwadi workers' stipends; Trump threatens to hit desalination plants if Hormuz isn't reopened more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top headlines: 1. Trump threatens to hit desalination plants if Hormuz not opened immediately On the 31st day of the US-Israel conflict with Iran, US President Donald Trump said the US is in “serious discussions” with a new Iranian regime. While noting “great progress,” he warned that if the Hormuz Strait remains closed, the US could target Iran’s electric plants, oil wells, Kharg Island, and desalination facilities in retaliation for past American deaths. 2. CM Yogi announces increase in Anganwadi stipends: Says, 'Honorarium should be 'smart'; 69,804 smartphones distributed to workers and helpers Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has announced that the stipend for Anganwadi workers and helpers will be increased, stressing that just as Anganwadi centers are becoming “smart,” their remuneration should also reflect modern standards. The announcement was made during a program where 69,804 smartphones were distributed to Anganwadi workers and chief helpers. 3. UP govt transfers 9 IAS officers in reshuffle: Anurag Yadav shifted after fallout of fake ₹25,000 crore MoU controversy The Uttar Pradesh Government carried out a late-night administrative reshuffle on Sunday, transferring nine IAS officers. Action was taken against the Principal Secretary of the IT and Electronics Department over a controversial ₹25,000 crore investment MoU that was later found to be dubious. 4. Rahul alleges only RSS will get foreign funds Elections in five states this April have intensified campaigning, with rallies and outreach drives underway. Mamata Banerjee accused the BJP of fuelling divisions. Rahul Gandhi, campaigning in Kerala, alleged Narendra Modi is under pressure from Donald Trump. 5. Grocer’s daughter secures second rank in UP PCS: Delhi’s Neha Panchal tops, new mother Shweta gets 21st rank The final result of UP PCS 2024 was released at 12:30 am on Sunday night. Neha Panchal from Delhi secured the top position. Ananya Trivedi from Raebareli stood second, and Abhay Pratap Singh ranked third. Six girls are among the top 10. Ananya’s father Sushil Trivedi runs a grocery shop. Her mother Rekha Rani is a government teacher. 6. Kanpur Zoo snakes have very expensive diet: Eat white rats as food worth ₹15 lakh every year; each feed costs ₹150 Around 50 venomous and non-venomous snakes at the Kanpur Zoo have a costly and carefully managed diet—white mice. According to zoo authorities, feeding these reptiles costs nearly ₹15 lakh annually, with each mouse priced at approximately ₹150. 7. Delhi Police arrest LeT-linked terrorist Security agencies in Delhi arrested Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) linked terrorist Shabbir Ahmad Lone from Delhi border on Monday. According to police, initial investigation has revealed that he was carrying out anti-India activities from Bangladesh. 8. Akhilesh focuses on 3 cr farmers, Gujjar-Muslim outreach: Experts say large crowd in BJP stronghold rally surprised observers, possible shift in western UP Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav addressed a 55-minute rally in Dadri constituency in Noida, marking an early pitch for the upcoming elections. His speech focused on farmers, women, and unemployment, with a key promise to offer market-rate compensation for land acquisition—an attempt to appeal to nearly 3 crore farmers in western Uttar Pradesh. The rally, titled “Samajwadi Samanta Bhaichara Rally,” was aimed at bridging the Hindu-Muslim divide and consolidating Gujjar and Muslim voters in the region. 9. Daughter-in-law not liable to support in-laws: Allahabad High Court rejects maintenance plea; Says, ‘No such legal provision exists’ The Allahabad High Court has dismissed a petition filed by an elderly couple seeking maintenance from their daughter-in-law. The court ruled that parents-in-law have no legal right to claim financial support from their daughter-in-law. 10. Sensex crashes 1,600 points, settles at over 2-year low; Nifty cracks nearly 500 points Indian benchmark indices extended losses on Monday, 30 March 2026. Sensex plunged 1,635.67 points to 71,947.55, marking its lowest close in over two years. Nifty fell over 2% to 22,331.40.

stories.title: Gorakhpur police nab 5 stunt performers:Accused involved in bike racing on roads, making videos for likes and views
stories.summary: Gorakhpur's Gulriha police station has taken 5 stunt performers into custody on Monday. Their 5 bikes have also been seized. Many videos of them performing stunts were being shared on social media. Many people had also complained about this. After which the police took action by identifying them through the related videos. CO Gorakhnath Ravi Kumar Singh said that a video of bike stunts in the Gulriha area on March 29 was going viral. In which it is clearly visible that life-threatening stunts are being performed with bikes on the road. The front wheel is also being lifted while riding the bike at high speed. The bike is being driven on one wheel. This video was going viral rapidly on social media. The public also gave sharp reactions to it. Taking cognizance of the video, police took 5 stunt performers including the bike into custody. They were identified as Shiva Mishra from Rakhokhor in Campeirganj, Ankit Kumar Verma from Dumri No. 2 in Gulriha, Adarsh Verma, Shakti Verma and Piyush Sonkar from Chiluatal Jhungia Bazar. Among them, Adarsh Verma and Shakti Verma are brothers. Make videos for reels During questioning, all five stunt performers revealed that they make videos to upload reels on Instagram. They perform dangerous stunts to get more likes and views. Gulriha Station Officer Ityanand Pandey reached with his team and apprehended all five youths.

stories.title: 3 lakh devotees reach Kashi Vishwanath Temple:Management makes elaborated arrangements, entry facilitated through 4 routes
stories.summary: At Shri Kashi Vishwanath Temple, a massive surge of faith and devotion was witnessed on Monday. With the start of the week, lakhs of devotees arrived in Kashi for darshan of Baba Vishwanath. Long queues formed in and around the temple premises since morning, immersing the entire area in a spiritual atmosphere. According to temple administration, more than 3 lakh devotees had already completed their darshan. Seeing the increasing crowd, the administration made special arrangements. Additional lines were set up for devotees' convenience to make the darshan process smooth and organized. See three pictures German hangers have been installed in the temple corridor to provide relief from intense heat and strong sunlight. Under these hangers, devotees are getting shade and comfort, which helps them stand in line for long periods without difficulty. Additionally, adequate arrangements have been made for drinking water and first aid. Entry being facilitated through 4 routes The administration has designated four separate routes to control the entry and exit of devotees. Through these paths, devotees are being allowed entry into the temple in a phased manner to prevent crowding and disorder. Strict arrangements have been made for security purposes. Police and security forces have been deployed throughout the area, while continuous monitoring is being done through CCTV cameras. Crowd increased due to school holidays and weekend Due to Sawan, Monday and weekend rush, there has been a tremendous increase in the number of devotees in Kashi. The administration claims that such crowds may continue in the coming days, for which all necessary preparations have been completed. Know what are the temple administration's arrangements due to increasing heat CEO Vishwa Bhushan Mishra said, “Devotees are coming to have darshan of Shri Vishwanath Mahadev in the summer. The temple trust has made all arrangements to protect devotees from intense sunlight and heat. German hangers have been arranged throughout the temple premises. Jute mats have been laid so that devotees' feet don't burn. These jute mats have been specially ordered from the Indian Jute Corporation Limited. Arrangements for drinking water, coolers, fans and ORS have also been made in the temple premises.”

stories.title: UP Merchant Navy officer freed from Iran jail:Reaches Mumbai via Dubai; wife alleges false oil smuggling case
stories.summary: The Iranian government has released 8 Indian nationals from jail, including Merchant Navy officer Anil Singh from Pratapgarh and Ketan Mehta from Ghaziabad. They were all arrested by the Iranian Navy on December 8, 2025, on charges of crude oil smuggling. A total of 16 Indians were arrested along with Anil and Ketan. 8 were released on December 23, 2025, while the remaining 8 Indians were released on February 26 after being held in jail for about four months. However, due to the Israel-Iran war, they could not immediately return to India. Finally, on Monday, they all arrived in Mumbai via Dubai. After reaching Mumbai, Navy officials have taken them into their custody. Anil Singh's wife Gayatri Devi said, “My husband was falsely implicated. The diesel smuggling charge was fake. The Iranian police had no evidence, yet everyone was kept in jail for so many days. With the help of PM Modi, Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar and other representatives, my husband and his other companions could be freed, I am heartily grateful to the government.” Complete matter in sequence On December 8, Iran's navy captured a merchant navy ship. The ship was loaded with several drums of crude oil. Anil's son Rituraj said, “For 4 days after the ship was captured, there was no contact with papa. After four days when papa was allowed to make a phone call, he called us and gave information about the whole matter. On January 8, he called again and told that we are all imprisoned in an Iranian jail.” Released on February 26, but remained stuck Rituraj said that he had sent an online letter to the Central Government and Ministry of External Affairs to get his father released from Iranian jail. He had also tweeted to PMO, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar and Ministry of External Affairs. The Iranian regime released Indians imprisoned on February 26. However, they remained stranded there due to the war starting from February 28. After the situation improved slightly, everyone was evacuated from there. They reached Mumbai from Dubai at around 5 am on Monday. Anil Singh is an officer in Dubai shipping company Anil's wife said, “My husband was an officer in a Dubai shipping company for many years. Last year suddenly we learned that he had been arrested. The ground slipped from under our feet upon hearing this news. We appealed for help. I am very happy that he is coming home.”

stories.title: Daughter-in-law not liable to support in-laws:Allahabad HC rejects elderly couple's maintenance plea; Says, 'No such legal provision exists'
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has dismissed a petition filed by an elderly couple seeking maintenance from their daughter-in-law. The court ruled that parents-in-law have no legal right to claim financial support from their daughter-in-law. The court observed that under Section 125 of the erstwhile Criminal Procedure Code, as well as the corresponding provisions of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, parents-in-law are not included among those entitled to maintenance. The order was passed by a single bench of Justice Madan Pal Singh. The case arose from a criminal revision petition filed by Rakesh Kumar and another resident of Agra. The couple had sought maintenance from their daughter-in-law under Section 144 following the death of their son. However, the Family Court had rejected their plea on 21 August 2025, prompting them to approach the High Court. After hearing arguments, the High Court noted that there was no evidence to show that the daughter-in-law had secured her job on compassionate grounds. It further stated that while a moral obligation may exist, it cannot be enforced as a legal duty. Maintenance can only be granted to those explicitly mentioned under the law. The petitioners’ counsel argued that the couple were illiterate and financially dependent on their only son, Pravesh Kumar, who served as a constable in the Uttar Pradesh Police. He died on 31 March 2021. His wife, also a constable in the police force, receives a stable income along with service and retirement benefits. The counsel contended that caring for parents-in-law should be treated as a legal responsibility. However, the court held that their claim under Section 144 was not legally sustainable, as the provision does not include parents-in-law among eligible dependents. It added that there was no error in the Family Court’s order. What Section 144 says: Under Section 144 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, a magistrate may direct a person with sufficient means to provide maintenance to a wife, children, or parents who are unable to support themselves.

stories.title: CM Yogi announces increase in Anganwadi stipends:Says, 'Honorarium should be 'smart'; 69,804 smartphones distributed to workers and helpers
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has announced that the stipend for Anganwadi workers and helpers will be increased, stressing that just as Anganwadi centers are becoming “smart,” their remuneration should also reflect modern standards. The announcement was made during a program where 69,804 smartphones were distributed to Anganwadi workers and chief helpers. Stipend to become “respectable and smart” CM Yogi said, “If an Anganwadi center is smart, then the stipend of workers should also be smart. I have instructed the department to complete their training promptly and propose a stipend hike. Once increased, it should be presented in a grand ceremony as a mark of respect. The minimum stipend must be guaranteed.” Targeting previous administrations, he added, “Before 2017, distribution of nutritional supplements was managed by liquor mafias who misappropriated funds and disrupted services meant for women and children. It was shocking that such people were infiltrating the Women and Child Development sector.” Smartphones and New infrastructure launched On Monday, CM Yogi addressed the program at Lok Bhawan, where the new design for Anganwadi centers was also unveiled. Over 200,000 growth monitoring devices were distributed, along with appointment letters for 18,440 Anganwadi workers and helpers. Additionally, CM Yogi inaugurated and laid the foundation for 3,170 Anganwadi center buildings and 140 child development project offices, totaling an investment of ₹450 crore. Ensuring fair recruitment and Ending exploitation The CM explained the reform in recruitment processes: earlier outsourced staff were often exploited by agencies and intermediaries who kept a majority of government salaries for themselves. Workers used to receive only ₹5,000–6,000 while agencies pocketed 10–12 thousand from the government. “We have established a corporation to manage outsourced employees, eliminating exploitation. A respectable stipend will empower workers to contribute to the state’s development and safeguard children’s futures,” said CM Yogi. Addressing malnutrition in Uttar Pradesh The CM highlighted the state’s poor nutrition scenario before 2017: “Nutritional supplements were often misappropriated by liquor mafias. Children remained malnourished, which impacted the overall health of the state.” Digital empowerment with smartphones CM Yogi added that over the last four years, he has focused on equipping every Anganwadi worker with smartphones to ensure real-time monitoring of activities. “This enables accurate data collection, improving rankings and program efficiency,” he said. New responsibilities under National Education Policy The Chief Minister stressed that Anganwadi centers will now cater to pre-primary education for children aged 3–5 years, as per the National Education Policy (NEP). Existing centers in school premises will be upgraded with new buildings to support pre-primary education. “You are in the role of Yashoda Maiya for these children, nurturing their growth and health. Your work ensures a bright future for India,” CM Yogi said. Minister Baby Rani Maurya highlights achievements Women and Child Development Minister Baby Rani Maurya said over 1.56 crore beneficiaries are receiving home-delivered nutritional supplements. She added that malnutrition among children has reduced by 6.6%. The minister also noted the appointment of over 19,000 new Anganwadi workers and promotion of more than 3,000 helpers. The distribution of 69,000+ smartphones marks the beginning of digital empowerment for Anganwadi workers.

stories.title: Kanpur Zoo snakes have very expensive diet:Eat white rats as food worth Rs 15 lakh every year; each feed costs ₹150
stories.summary: Around 50 venomous and non-venomous snakes at the Kanpur Zoo have a costly and carefully managed diet—white mice. According to zoo authorities, feeding these reptiles costs nearly ₹15 lakh annually, with each mouse priced at approximately ₹150. Diet based on size and health Zoo officials state that a healthy snake is fed one to three mice depending on its size. The mice are sourced from registered suppliers to ensure they are safe, disease-free, and suitable for consumption. Seasonal feeding pattern Dr. Kanhaiya Patel, Director of Kanpur Zoo, explained that snakes’ feeding habits vary with the seasons. During the three winter months, snakes go into hibernation and do not eat at all. However, as temperatures rise and snakes become active, their feeding schedule resumes. Currently, about 50 mice are procured weekly. Feeding typically takes place on Saturdays, allowing the snakes ample time to digest their food undisturbed, especially since the zoo remains closed on Mondays. Annual consumption crosses 10,000 mice During the summer season, the zoo uses around 320 mice per month. Over the course of a year, the total consumption reaches approximately 10,250 white mice. With each mouse costing around ₹150, the total annual expense exceeds ₹15 lakh—a figure that may seem surprising but is considered necessary by wildlife experts. Why white mice are preferred White mice are chosen over wild rodents for several important reasons. They are easier for snakes to digest and are bred in controlled lab or farm environments, making them free from diseases and parasites. Additionally, they offer a balanced nutritional profile, rich in calcium and protein, which is essential for the snakes’ growth and health. Preserving natural hunting instincts Feeding live or appropriately sized mice also helps maintain the snakes’ natural hunting instincts. Depending on the size of the snake, anything from small to adult mice is selected to meet their dietary needs and support their overall well-being.

stories.title: Akhilesh targets 3 crore farmers, Gujjar-Muslim voters:Big crowd in BJP stronghold signals shift in western UP
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav addressed a 55-minute rally in Dadri constituency in Noida, marking an early pitch for the upcoming elections. His speech focused on farmers, women, and unemployment, with a key promise to offer market-rate compensation for land acquisition—an attempt to appeal to nearly 3 crore farmers in western Uttar Pradesh. The rally, titled “Samajwadi Samanta Bhaichara Rally,” was aimed at bridging the Hindu-Muslim divide and consolidating Gujjar and Muslim voters in the region. Despite the Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD), led by Jayant Chaudhary, exiting the alliance ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls, the Samajwadi Party performed well in several constituencies, including Muzaffarnagar and Kairana. In the 2022 assembly elections, SP and RLD won 43 seats, while BJP candidates were successful in 93 seats. SP is pushing hard to change this figure. Which equations did Akhilesh Yadav target in West UP? Find out in this report… Outreach in Gujjar belt signals broader strategy The rally in a Gujjar-dominated region indicated the party’s push to expand its base in western UP. The Samajwadi Party is attempting to rebuild alliances among communities that drifted apart after the 2013 riots. In the 2022 Assembly elections, the Samajwadi-RLD alliance won 43 seats, while BJP secured 93 out of 136 seats in the region. The party is now working to alter this equation. Mihir Bhoj statue promise targets Gujjar sentiment Akhilesh Yadav announced that a statue of Mihir Bhoj would be installed at the riverfront in Lucknow. The move is seen as an effort to connect with the Gujjar community, which regards Mihir Bhoj as a key historical figure. The announcement also aligns with SP’s broader non-Yadav OBC outreach strategy, positioning the party as one that respects community identity and history. Criticism of BJP’s development model Akhilesh questioned the BJP government’s claims on infrastructure and development, particularly airport connectivity. He alleged that several inaugurated airports were non-functional and accused the government of promoting “hollow” development narratives. He also claimed that projects like metro expansion and connectivity improvements were initiated during the SP government, not the BJP administration. Farmers remain central to strategy From the rally stage, Akhilesh targeted farmers across districts like Muzaffarnagar, Baghpat, Shamli, Meerut, Bijnor, and Bulandshahr—regions where agricultural issues significantly influence electoral outcomes. He promised that if the Samajwadi forms the government, land acquisition would be compensated at market rates, alleging that current policies undervalue farmers’ land. Jobs, women welfare, and MoU criticism Akhilesh pledged a focus on employment for youth and announced financial assistance of ₹40,000 annually for women under a proposed welfare scheme. He also criticized the government over large investment MoUs that allegedly failed to generate corresponding employment, a point that resonated with the crowd. Expert views: PDA formula showing impact Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans said the rally could be considered successful, especially in terms of crowd turnout in a non-election period. He noted that Akhilesh’s PDA (Backward, Dalit, Minority) strategy appears to be gaining traction and that mobilizing such crowds in a BJP stronghold reflects political momentum. BJP responds, questions Samajwadi’s track record BJP spokesperson Avneesh Tyagi countered that despite extensive campaigning, the rally turnout fell short of expectations. He emphasized BJP’s development projects, citing infrastructure initiatives like the Delhi-Meerut rapid rail and new airport projects, and argued that SP lacks comparable achievements in the region. SP reaffirms focus on 2027 elections Samajwadi spokesperson Ameek Jamei said the party has a clear roadmap focused on youth, women, and farmers ahead of the 2027 elections. He added that upcoming rallies will further outline the party’s development agenda for Uttar Pradesh.
