stories.title: Grocer’s daughter secures second rank in UP PCS:Delhi’s Neha Panchal tops, new mother Shweta gets 21st rank
stories.summary: The final result of UP PCS 2024 was released at 12:30 am on Sunday night. Neha Panchal from Delhi secured the top position. Ananya Trivedi from Raebareli stood second, and Abhay Pratap Singh ranked third. Six girls are among the top 10. Ananya’s father Sushil Trivedi runs a grocery shop. Her mother Rekha Rani is a government teacher. Her maternal uncle Rajesh Pandey is an Additional SP in Kanpur Dehat. Ananya cleared the exam in her first attempt. Meanwhile, Neha Panchal qualified the exam in her fourth attempt. Shweta Verma from Kanpur secured the 21st rank. She became a mother four months ago. Her father Jagdish Verma retired as a cashier from a bank. Ananya Trivedi, Rank-2: Father's grocery shop, mother government teacher A total of 932 candidates have been selected, including 319 girls. Among the selected candidates, 37 have been appointed as Deputy Collectors (SDM), 17 as Deputy Superintendents of Police (DSP), and 196 as Assistant Commissioners (Commercial Tax). Talking about PCS 2023, Siddharth Gupta from Saharanpur had topped the exam. Only two girls were in the top 10. No suitable candidates were found for 14 posts. For 947 posts, 2,719 candidates were called for interviews. Out of them, 2,698 appeared, while 21 did not. Fourteen posts of Vyavasthadhikari and one more administrative post remained vacant due to the lack of eligible candidates. For PCS 2024 Prelims, 5.76 lakh candidates had applied. The prelims result was declared in March 2025. Out of these, 15,066 candidates qualified for the mains. A total of 13,776 candidates appeared in the mains exam, which was conducted between June 29 and July 2, 2025. Abhishek Singh from Gonda has secured 68th rank. He has become Assistant Commissioner GST. Abhishek is from Ata Parsapur. His father Chandra Pratap Singh and mother Kiran Singh are Head Masters in Junior High School. Abhishek Singh is currently posted in the IB department in Delhi. Read the interview of second-rank holder Ananya Trivedi: You have secured the second rank in PCS. What would you like to say? Initially, there were many new challenges, but my parents always supported me. I come from a rural background. Facilities were limited in the village, so the struggle was greater. I studied in a public school in Raebareli city. In the initial years, commuting was difficult. How did you start your preparation? I completed Sociology Honours from BHU and was a gold medallist. After that, I started preparing for civil services. This was my first mains and first interview in UPPCS. I got the second rank. It still feels unbelievable. Did you take coaching? I never took coaching and relied on self-study. However, I did take guidance from my maternal uncle, who is an Additional SP. Nowadays, with the help of ChatGPT and the internet, content on any topic is easily available. Your uncle is an Additional SP. Are you influenced by him? His life story inspires me because he has achieved this position through great struggle. The decision to join civil services was my own. My family never pressured me. Did you want to join civil services since childhood? I studied PCM (Physics, Chemistry, Maths) till Class 12. I never wanted to become an engineer or doctor. I like working with the public in civil services. It is not my final goal, but a platform to start my career. What message would you like to give to aspirants? If you work honestly in anything and stay true to your family and responsibilities, God rewards you with success. I would like to tell aspirants to work hard; success will surely come. What her parents said: Why did you move from the village to Raebareli city? Father: There were limited facilities for commuting from the village, so we settled in Raebareli. My daughter always performed well in every class, so I wanted to ensure her education faced no problems. What challenges did you face in your children’s education? Mother: There were some difficulties, but the children remained disciplined. The home environment was conducive to studies. My daughter worked hard and became self-reliant. When the rank came, we couldn’t believe it at first. We checked the roll number and then realised it was God’s blessing.

stories.title: UP govt transfers 9 IAS officers in reshuffle:Anurag Yadav shifted after fallout of fake ₹25,000 crore MoU controversy
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Government carried out a late-night administrative reshuffle on Sunday, transferring nine IAS officers. Action was taken against the Principal Secretary of the IT and Electronics Department over a controversial ₹25,000 crore investment MoU that was later found to be dubious. Action over alleged fake investment MoU The state government removed Anurag Yadav from the IT and Electronics Department and posted him as Principal Secretary in the Social Welfare and Sainik Welfare Departments. The controversy stemmed from an MoU signed by a company identified as “AI Puch,” which had claimed an investment of ₹25,000 crore in the state. The agreement had initially been praised by the government. However, it later emerged that the company’s net worth was not even ₹50 crore. After the MoU went viral on social media, Invest UP cancelled the agreement. Despite IT Minister Sunil Sharma stating that the MoU was executed at the level of Invest UP without his knowledge, the government held Anurag Yadav accountable as the department’s Principal Secretary and removed him. M. Devaraj gets additional charge M. Devaraj, Principal Secretary of the Appointment and Personnel Department, has been given additional charge as Director General of the UP Academy of Administration and Management, along with his current responsibilities. He had earlier been removed as Principal Secretary of the Tax Department after GST collections in the state declined. Alok Kumar Tritiya gets IT department charge Alok Kumar Tritiya, considered close to Chief Secretary S. P. Goyal, has been assigned additional charge as Principal Secretary of the IT and Electronics Department along with his current role in the Planning Department. Other key transfers See full list

stories.title: 4 terrorists arrested in Lucknow over blast plot:Gang leader from Meerut; Pakistan-based handlers assigned targets for attacks
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) has arrested four suspected terrorists in Lucknow, officials confirmed on Friday. According to the ATS, the group was allegedly planning arson and terror attacks across India under the direction of handlers based in Pakistan. The accused have been identified as Saqib alias Devil, Vikas Gehlawat alias Raunak, Lokesh alias Babu, also known as Papla Pandit, and Arbab. Saqib is believed to be the leader of the group. From their possession, ATS recovered a chemical-filled container, seven mobile phones, 24 pamphlets, and Aadhaar cards. Investigators are analysing key digital evidence found on the seized devices. Plan to target Lucknow Railway Station The ATS revealed that the group had planned to target infrastructure near Lucknow Railway Station, including damaging the railway signal box. The intention was to trigger a major explosion and cause significant casualties on 2 April, thereby spreading panic. Acting on prior intelligence, ATS teams intervened in time and apprehended the suspects before the plan could be executed. Links to Pakistan and foreign networks Preliminary investigation indicates that the group was in contact with Pakistani handlers through social media and encrypted communication platforms. Saqib, a resident of Agwanpur village in Meerut who worked as a barber, is said to have established these connections. He reportedly communicated with handlers via platforms such as Telegram, Instagram, and Signal. Authorities also found links to suspicious foreign numbers, including some believed to be based in Afghanistan. These platforms were allegedly used for secure coordination of anti-national activities. Network built through local recruitment Investigators said Saqib expanded the network by recruiting acquaintances. He first involved Arbab, who is from his village, and later brought in Vikas Gehlawat and Lokesh, both residents of Gautam Buddh Nagar, through online contact. Officials believe that financial incentives and exposure to radical content motivated the accused to join the network. The group had reportedly been conducting reconnaissance at various locations. Reconnaissance and target identification The primary objective of the group was to create fear and instability. For this purpose, they carried out reconnaissance of key locations, including prominent institutions, crowded public areas, vehicles, and railway infrastructure. Cities such as Ghaziabad, Aligarh, and Lucknow were among the locations surveyed. Pakistani handlers allegedly shared specific locations via Google Maps, which the accused would visit and document through videos before sending detailed reports back. Use of arson and financial incentives During interrogation, it emerged that the accused carried out small-scale arson incidents to demonstrate their activities. These acts were recorded and shared with handlers in Pakistan as proof. In return, payments were reportedly made through QR code-based transactions. Authorities believe this financial arrangement played a role in sustaining the network’s operations. Radicalisation and intent to disrupt peace Investigators also found that the accused were exposed to radical ideologies through online groups linked to extremist organisations. They were allegedly encouraged to carry out acts of violence and arson in the name of religion. According to the ATS, the overarching aim was to spread fear, fuel communal tension, and disrupt internal peace and security across the country.

stories.title: Yogi praises Ranveer Singh’s Dhurandhar in Kashi:Says films now portray ‘dacoits’ differently; MP CM Mohan Yadav gifts Vedic clock
stories.summary: During the grand theatrical presentation of Vikramotsav 2026 in Kashi on Friday, Yogi Adityanath praised Dhurandhar, starring Ranveer Singh, saying today’s films now portray what is right correctly, unlike earlier, when right and wrong were often reversed. The program was inaugurated by Yogi Adityanath, Mohan Yadav, and Gajendra Singh Shekhawat. Mohan Yadav also presented a Vedic clock to Yogi, which will be installed at Kashi Vishwanath Temple on Saturday. The clock follows Indian time calculation, dividing the day into 30 Muhurtas. The event began with Mridang sounds, featured 21 artists performing Matka dance, and involved over 200 artists, with live elements including 8 horses, 2 chariots, 4 camels, 1 palanquin, and 1 elephant. stories.title: First N-Gen Post Office opens in Varanasi:Cafe-like feel and digital services at one place give full comfort
stories.summary: The N-Gen (Next Generation) Post Office has been inaugurated at the Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith campus in Varanasi. This is the first N-Gen Post Office in the Varanasi region, which has been designed keeping in mind the needs of youth and students. It was inaugurated by the university's Vice-Chancellor Professor Anand Kumar Tyagi and Postmaster General Padmagandha Mishra. The interior of this N-Gen has been designed in a cafe style, providing facilities to sit and work and spend time. Options like a mini library, TV, video games, chess and carrom are also available for students. Additionally, free Wi-Fi facility has been provided so that students can easily do their studies and other online work. The walls and seating arrangement have been designed in such a way that this place looks less like an official office and more like a youth zone. Here, along with postal services, facilities of digital banking, e-commerce logistics and India Post Payments Bank are also available at one place. This means if a student needs to send money, open an account or get information related to online orders, there is no need to go to different places. During the inauguration, Postmaster General Padmagandha Mishra said that this initiative has been started keeping youth in mind, so that they can connect with new technology along with postal services. Vice Chancellor Professor Anand Kumar Tyagi said that with the start of such a facility in the university, the connection between students and the postal department will be strengthened and they will get the benefit of new facilities. Khushi Rai, a BA third-year student at Kashi Vidyapeeth, appreciated this initiative and said that this post office is very useful for students. She mentioned that the atmosphere here is very good and students can sit here and get information related to their postal and banking needs, among other requirements. According to students, this N-Gen Post Office has now emerged as a new center of new facilities, better services and modern environment for the youth.

stories.title: No one can read namaz on roads':UP CM Yogi says in Asam rally, 'Rioters' property is distributed among poor'
stories.summary: 'We used to say that Ram Lalla, we will come and build the temple there. Congress said that Ram never existed. Congress's allies worked to deny Ram's existence. But under the BJP's double-engine government, a grand Ram temple has been constructed in Ayodhya. Now, there is no curfew in UP. No curfew, no riots, everything is fine in UP. No one can offer namaz on the streets. There is no sound of shouting from any religion. If anyone dares to riot, their property is confiscated and distributed among the poor and Dalits.' These statements were made by CM Yogi on Friday during the assembly election campaign in Assam. He had arrived to hold a rally in support of NDA candidate Deepak Kumar Das for the Barpeta assembly seat. 1. 'Congress allies worked to deny Ram's existence' Yogi said that the double-engine government respects heritage. Only a double-engine government can do this. Wherever there is a BJP government, work has been shown. There was a movement for Shri Ram Janmabhoomi in Ayodhya; people used to come from Assam too. We used to say that we would come to Ramlala, we would build the temple there. Congress used to say that Ram never existed. Congress allies have worked to deny Ram's existence. But, under the BJP's double-engine government, a grand Ram temple has been constructed in Ayodhya. 2. 'Will not let the conspiracy of Congress and UDF succeed' The CM said that Congress and UDF tampered with the culture of Assam. They worked to spoil the demography here by infiltrating infiltrators. They attempted to forcibly occupy the houses and land of the people of Assam. On one hand, the government under the leadership of Himanta Biswa Sarma is working to advance development and heritage. Arrangements are also being made to identify each and every infiltrator and remove them from here. On the other hand, major development works are also being witnessed in Assam. stories.title: Minors involved in Agra nude video scandal were friends:Aged between 14-17; boys sent to juvenile home, girls undergoing counselling
stories.summary: The Khandoli area of Agra suddenly came into focus on March 31 after 48 obscene videos were circulated on social media. The clips showed three boys and two girls, all aged between 14 and 17. The videos went viral at a time when the Shri Ram fair was underway in the area, leading to tension. Although no formal complaint was filed, police took cognisance and arrested two boys. During the probe, it emerged that the girls belong to Hindu families, while one of the boys is Muslim. Following this, 48 police personnel were deployed in the area. All those involved are minors, so police are proceeding cautiously. The arrested boys have been sent to a juvenile home, while both girls are undergoing counselling. It has come to light that all five knew each other and whatever is seen in the videos was consensual. Questions have arisen over how the videos suddenly surfaced, why they were made, who leaked them and what options the police now have. Minister inaugurated the fair, obscene videos spread at the fair Khandoli is located around 20 km from the Agra district headquarters. The 126th historic Shri Ram fair and wrestling event is currently underway there. It was inaugurated on March 26 by Union Minister of State Prof SP Singh Baghel. Until then, the fair was the main attraction, but the situation changed on March 31. Videos began circulating among people at the fair. The clips showed two girls and three boys in an explicit state. By 9 am, the videos had started spreading rapidly, and by noon, they had reached almost everyone in the area. Locals identified the boys in the videos as residents of the same village. One boy is Muslim, while the others belong to Maurya and Kashyap communities. Of the two girls seen in the videos, one belongs to the Thakur community and the other to the OBC category. Both are from different villages. All were studying in classes 9 to 12, except the Muslim boy, who had dropped out and was working at a shop. Friendship through social media, then started meeting each other Residents of the villages said the group already knew each other and later connected on Instagram, where they used to communicate. They exchanged photos and videos. Being young, they engaged in showing off, forming relationships and recording videos. They were often seen roaming together in the locality. Planned to meet 3 months ago, then made nude videos The sequence began around three months ago when the five planned to meet. They chose a friend’s house as the location and gathered there. At the house, they recorded explicit videos. No force or coercion is visible in the clips. Some videos are around 30 seconds long, while others are 10–15 seconds. Two girls and two boys are seen in compromising acts, while the third boy recorded the videos. Where the incident occurred, there have been disturbances before as well Locals said the area has a significant Thakur population and has witnessed disputes earlier. After the incident, tension increased, prompting the administration to go on alert and deploy police. One reason cited is that one of the accused boys belongs to the Muslim community and appears in the videos. Movement near his house has been restricted. After the videos surfaced, families of those involved confined themselves indoors. No one lodged a complaint, but police understood the seriousness and registered an FIR on their own, arresting two boys. Station House Officer Kuldeep Singh said that if the girls’ families file a complaint, further charges will be added. For now, an FIR has been registered under sections related to uploading obscene content on digital platforms. Sold the mobile, that's why the videos came out During questioning, one of the boys told police that the videos were stored on his phone, which he later sold without deleting the data, leading to their circulation. However, he could not clearly explain when and to whom the phone was sold. His statements also contained contradictions. He also failed to explain what other data was stored on the device. Police suspect there may be more to the case. Two different locations are visible in the videos, suggesting they may have been recorded at separate places. There are 6 more questions before the police, which are being investigated... DCP said- Appeal to people, don't share these videos DCP of Agra West, Aditya Singh said- All the boys and girls involved in this are minors. The videos that are currently going viral are all from 3 months ago. Two boys have been arrested so far. During interrogation, it was also revealed that all of them were previously acquainted with each other. The DCP also appealed to people that if you have the video, do not share it. Action can be taken for sharing it.

stories.title: Woman who robbed jewellery shop in Ayodhya in Burqa arrested:Turns out to be Hindu girl; 4-month-old pregnant lady used fake gun for robbery
stories.summary: Police in Ayodhya have arrested a 25-year-old woman and her 27-year-old accomplice late on Thursday night for carrying out a robbery at a jewellery shop while disguised in a burqa. The accused have been identified as Payal and her friend Rahul, who was waiting on a motorcycle some distance away during the incident. Payal fled the scene and escaped with Rahul. Police investigation revealed that Rahul had purchased a fake pistol and a burqa from the market. Payal reached the shop around 12:30 pm wearing the burqa and used the fake weapon to rob a gold necklace and chain worth around ₹3.6 lakh. The duo had planned the crime using the burqa to conceal identity. The incident took place in the Kothi Bazaar area under Rudauli police station limits. The entire act was captured on six CCTV cameras installed at the shop. The registration number of the motorcycle used in the escape was also recorded, which helped police trace and arrest both accused. ADG Zone Lucknow Praveen Kumar informed- Two people have been arrested. The name of the girl who committed the robbery wearing a burqa is Payal. The name of the boy who was with her is Rahul. Both were executing the incident by becoming Bunty and Babli. Both are friends. The robbery was carried out by showing a toy pistol. Now read the complete matter in detail... She came wearing a burqa to buy a gold necklace and chain Mahesh, a gold and silver trader from Kothi Bazaar, runs Mahesh Jewellers located about 900 metres from his residence in Agrawal Complex. On Thursday, Payal, a resident of Ahibaran ka Purwa in Mathana Nivada gram panchayat, arrived at the shop along with her friend Rahul from Paran ka Purwa village. Payal entered the shop alone wearing a burqa and carrying a backpack, while Rahul stayed back at a distance. She told Mahesh that she wanted to purchase a gold necklace and chain, following which he placed both items before her. She then asked for water. Mahesh sent his employee Ankit Kumar to bring water and samosas. After Ankit returned, Payal refused to eat the samosa but took the water bottle. Said - I don't eat samosas, please get me sweets Payal then said she does not eat samosas and asked for sweets. Mahesh sent Ankit again to bring barfi. During this time, another employee, Maniram, placed the necklace and chain on the counter. Payal stood up and started moving around inside the shop. When Mahesh asked her what she was looking for, she replied that her husband had gone to withdraw money and she was waiting for him. She then stood near the counter. As Mahesh got busy arranging other items in the cupboard, Payal picked up the gold necklace and chain from the box and lifted her bag. Pulled out pistol from waist, said- If you move forward, I will shoot When the shopkeeper tried to stop her, she pulled out a pistol from her waist, pointed it at him and threatened to shoot if he moved forward. She then ran out of the shop. Mahesh and Maniram chased her, raising an alarm. Payal ran on foot and escaped with Rahul, who was waiting on a motorcycle a short distance away. According to Mahesh, the necklace weighed 26 grams (22 carat) and was valued at around ₹3.6 lakh as per market rates on April 2. Know about the accused- Payal’s father, Ramkeval, runs a laundry centre named after her. She is the third among four sisters; the eldest is married, while the other two live at home. Rahul lives about 16 km away from Payal’s residence. Rahul, a resident of Paran ka Purwa in Nevra gram panchayat, had lost his father Radheshyam some time ago. He is the youngest of three brothers. His elder brother Lavkush stays at home, while another brother, Bablu, works as a labourer in Delhi. Rahul lives separately.

stories.title: Seema Haider names son ‘Bharat’:Says, 'Proud to be Hindu in India, do not want to return to Pakistan'
stories.summary: Seema Haider, who came to India from Pakistan, has named her newborn son ‘Bharat’. The naming ceremony was held on Thursday at her residence in Rabupura, Noida. Seema said Hinduism is very beautiful and she feels proud to be a Hindu. Seema Haider said- I support India in cricket matches. When India wins a match, I feel happy. During the match, I pray to God that India should win. The people of India are very good. I don't want to go back to Pakistan. People of every caste live here. They love me, respect me. They consider me their daughter-in-law. In fact, this is Seema Haider’s sixth child, whom she gave birth to on February 18, 2026, at a hospital in Noida. Earlier, she had also given birth to a daughter. Seema has four children from her Pakistani husband, while she has two children with her Indian husband Sachin Meena. When the priest suggested the name, it came with the letter ‘Bh’ Seema Haider said that when the priest suggested a name, it started with the letter ‘Bha’. After much thought, the name ‘Bharat’ was chosen. She said there could be no better name than Bharat. She added that she is very happy after coming to India and has never regretted leaving Pakistan. Seema has 2 million followers on YouTube channel- Seema creates videos with her husband Sachin. She has been living with him in Rabupura, Noida, since 2023. Their story has remained widely discussed. The couple is very active on social media. Their YouTube channel has more than 2 million followers. Love through PUBG game, came to India via Nepal Seema Haider married Ghulam Haider in 2014. In 2019, Ghulam Haider moved to Dubai, leaving Seema and their four children in Karachi. That same year, Seema met Sachin Meena from Rabupura, Noida, online while playing PUBG. On March 10, 2023, Seema and Sachin met in person in Nepal. They claimed to have converted religion and married in a temple there. After that, Seema returned to Pakistan while Sachin came back to Noida. On May 13, Seema again travelled from Pakistan to Nepal via Dubai and then reached Rabupura by bus. On July 1, Seema and Sachin met a lawyer in Bulandshahr to get Indian identity documents prepared. The lawyer informed the police about Seema being a Pakistani national. Sachin-Seema were taken into custody from Haryana After this, both went absconding. On July 3, Seema and Sachin were taken into custody from Ballabhgarh in Haryana. On July 4, 2023, Sachin’s father Netrapal was arrested by the police. On July 8, all three were granted bail by the court. On July 17 and 18, the ATS questioned Seema and Sachin. On July 21, 2023, photos and videos of their wedding surfaced. Filed petition with the President for citizenship On July 21, 2023, Seema filed a petition with the President seeking Indian citizenship. On July 23, after questioning Sachin’s cousin in Bulandshahr, two youths from Ahmedgarh were detained and later arrested. On July 30, 2023, Seema released a video appealing for help, saying she did not even have money for food. On August 2, filmmaker Amit Jani from Meerut announced a film titled ‘Karachi to Noida’ based on Seema and Sachin, and a promo shoot was done. However, the film has not been completed yet.

stories.title: Kanpur’s cross-border kidney transplant racket:African woman pays ₹2.5 Cr for surgery; several hospitals in spotlight
stories.summary: The Kanpur kidney transplant racket has links not only within Uttar Pradesh but also abroad. Foreign patients were secretly coming here for illegal kidney transplants. The traffickers had formed a panel of hospitals and doctors across several states, including Delhi, Mumbai and West Bengal, to carry out the operations. After finalising deals with both donors and recipients, the gang conducted illegal kidney transplants at different locations across the country. Which hospital would be used, which doctors’ team would perform the transplant, and who the donor and recipient were—everything was kept secret. Separate individuals handled each responsibility. The doctors’ team would arrive by flight, complete the transplant within a few hours, and leave. So far, 8 arrests have been made in the case. How the kidney transplant racket was operating and what its international links are—here is what the arrested OT technicians told. OT Technician Spills the Beans - Conducted Transplants in Several States Kanpur DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said that six accused have already been sent to jail. On April 2, two OT technicians—Kuldeep Singh Raghav and Rajesh Kumar—were arrested. Rajesh is a resident of Ghaziabad and works as an OT technician at Sarvodaya Hospital in Noida, while Kuldeep Singh Raghav is from Pilkhuwa in Hapur and works at Shanti Gopal Hospital. During questioning, both revealed that a doctor named Rohit from Noida used to send them for kidney transplant cases. Along with them, a urologist would also travel from Delhi to Kanpur by flight for the transplant. They were paid between ₹35,000 and ₹50,000 for each case. Transplant of South African Woman Performed According to DCP Qasim Abidi, the technicians revealed that they were involved not only in Kanpur cases but also in the transplant of a South African woman named Arabica. The gang carried out kidney transplants not only in Kanpur but also in Delhi, Meerut, Noida, West Bengal and Haryana. Doctor Rohit from Noida had created a panel of hospitals in every state. For example, in Kanpur alone, he had six hospitals in his panel. All operations in Kanpur and nearby districts were handled by Shivam Agarwal alias Shivam Kada. Panel of 8 doctors, flight arrangements The gang had formed a panel of eight doctors. Wherever a transplant had to be carried out, Dr Rohit arranged flight travel for all of them. In Kanpur too, in a similar manner, on the night of March 29 at 9 pm, a kidney from Ayush was transplanted into Parul Tomar from Muzaffarnagar. Doctors would reach the concerned city directly by flight, perform the transplant, and then leave. Keeping Donor-Receiver Names Secret DCP West SM Qasim Abidi said the entire operation was run like a secret mission. The identities of the doctors performing the transplant, the donor and recipient, and the hospital where the transplant was to take place were all kept confidential. The entire work was handled by different teams. For example, Parul Tomar, a resident of North Civil Lines in Muzaffarnagar, had struck a deal with Dr Afzal from Meerut. Meanwhile, Ayush Kumar, an MBA student from Bihar studying in Dehradun, had finalised a deal to sell his kidney with Shivam Agarwal alias Shivam Kada of Kanpur. Both were in contact with absconding Noida-based doctor Rohit. Foreigners' Kidneys Replaced for Up to 2.50 Crores According to the police, within India, kidney transplants were carried out for ₹60 lakh to ₹1 crore. However, foreign patients were charged up to ₹2.5 crore. Evidence has been found showing that the kidney transplant of the South African woman Arabica was done for ₹2 crore to ₹2.5 crore. The syndicate has carried out not just a few but hundreds of kidney transplants. More than 50 people, including brokers and doctors, are believed to be involved in this network. Police teams are conducting raids from Kanpur to Meerut, Lucknow, Delhi, Noida and Ghaziabad. Know About Police Action Kanpur Police have so far arrested 8 accused in this case. DCP West said that after the racket was exposed, CCTV footage of people visiting Ahuja Hospital on the night of March 29 was examined. Two cars were used to transport doctors—one carrying five doctors and the other three. Three doctors were dropped in Ghaziabad, while five were dropped in Lucknow. Police are also examining further CCTV footage. So far, the investigation has revealed that Noida-based Dr Rohit alias Rahul and three Meerut-based doctors—Dr Afzal, Dr Vaibhav and Dr Anurag alias Amit—are involved in the gang. All their names are mentioned in the FIR, and police teams are conducting raids to arrest them. Know about the Meerut hospital to which the links are being traced During the investigation of the Kanpur kidney case, it has emerged that more than 100 transplants were carried out at Alpha Hospital in Meerut. The hospital is located in Mangal Pandey Nagar and is built on about 350 square yards. The building has four floors. The director of the hospital is Amit Kumar. The hospital management and staff claim that no doctor named Afzal is associated with them. According to the manager, only regular OPD services by Dr Vaibhav Mugdal are conducted, while other doctors are called on demand. At present, police are questioning the manager and continuing the investigation. Alpha Hospital was in the news before as well Meanwhile, Meerut's CMO Dr. Ashok Kataria says that on November 26, 2025, a patient complained that he was admitted after taking commission. The hospital's license was suspended on this. The police investigation did not confirm the allegation. The license was restored on January 21, 2026.

stories.title: Government to release 81,000 police vacancies in UP:CM Yogi stresses timely recruitment, orders reshuffle of long-posted staff
stories.summary: More than 81,000 vacancies will be filled in the Uttar Pradesh Police. The announcement was made by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath during a late-night review meeting of the police department on Thursday. The Chief Minister said that 2026–27 will be very important for youth preparing to join the Uttar Pradesh Police. Preparations are underway to recruit over 81,000 personnel within a year. He also directed officials to further strengthen law and order. He said police personnel posted for a long time in places like Raj Bhavan, the Chief Minister’s residence and police headquarters in Lucknow should be transferred. He asked officials to adopt a result-oriented approach and ensure accountability at every level. Recruitment will be conducted for these positions Officials informed the Chief Minister that recruitment will be conducted for more than 81,000 posts across various categories, including Sub-Inspectors, constables, radio assistant operators, computer operator Grade-A and confidential Sub-Inspectors. The recruitment process for some posts has already begun. The Chief Minister directed the Uttar Pradesh Police Recruitment and Promotion Board to ensure that all direct recruitments are conducted transparently, fairly and in accordance with reservation rules, within a fixed timeline. He emphasised the use of technology to complete the process on time and strengthen trust among youth. stories.title: Bareilly professor breaks silence on ‘sexy’ remark row:Alleges attack by hired goons, says, 'Will continue writing on flaws in govt and system'
stories.summary: A controversy at Bareilly College has intensified after Professor Alok Kumar Khare, accused of making an objectionable social media remark about a BJP woman leader, alleged that he was attacked by “hired goons” and vowed to continue writing about systemic shortcomings. Speaking in an exclusive interview with Dainik Bhaskar, Khare said, “ABVP used to be a good organisation, but now indisciplined elements are being recruited. Some hired miscreants even tried to attack me. I am not anti-government, but I will keep writing about flaws in the system.” What triggered the controversy The row began when Khare, then Chief Proctor of Bareilly College, shared a social media post commenting on BJP leader Komapella Madhavi Latha in a derogatory manner. The post quickly went viral, sparking outrage among student groups, especially members of the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP). On April 1, ABVP workers stormed the principal’s office, raised slogans, and allegedly manhandled Khare. The situation escalated to the point where some female students reportedly attempted to assault him. Amid rising tensions, Principal Dr. Om Prakash Rai removed Khare from the post of Chief Proctor and dissolved the entire proctorial board. ‘This was a planned conspiracy’ Khare claimed the incident was premeditated, The social media post was just an excuse. A conspiracy was hatched with the help of some insiders on campus to target and humiliate me. I had already submitted my resignation three days earlier. He alleged that external elements were brought in, Students of this campus would never stoop to grabbing a teacher by the collar. These were outsiders. We are reviewing CCTV footage and will take legal action. Allegations against ABVP The professor criticized ABVP’s recent functioning, Earlier, ABVP had disciplined members. Now, unruly individuals have entered the organization. Many of those present during the incident were not even members. He further alleged that political backing emboldens such behavior, When those in power offer protection, taking legal action becomes difficult. This increases their confidence. Fear for life, demands action Khare expressed concern for his safety, If they can behave like this with the Chief Proctor, they can do anything. I’ve been warned not to move alone on campus. There is a real threat to my life. He said a formal complaint has been submitted and action is awaited, If no action is taken in two to three days, we will protest and approach higher authorities. Clarification on social media post Defending himself, Khare said, I am a science teacher and often write against superstition. I did not even know who the woman was. If someone had objected, they could have approached me. I would have apologized. Violence is not justified. ‘I am not anti-government’ Responding to allegations of being anti-government, Khare stated, I do not write against the government, but I do highlight flaws in the system. Law and order may have improved, but issues in education remain. He added that raising concerns—such as pollution or problems faced by farmers—should not be seen as opposition but as stating facts. A career marked by controversy Professor Khare has a teaching career spanning over 35 years. He completed his graduation in 1984 from YD College, Lakhimpur Kheri, and later earned a PhD in Botany. Before joining Bareilly College, he taught at Sacred Heart Degree College in Sitapur and is also an authorized research supervisor at Rohilkhand University. However, he has frequently been in the spotlight due to his outspoken social media posts.

stories.summary: A spectacular drone show lit up Belfast's night sky, forming the outline of the historic RMS Titanic. Around 950 drones created the glowing silhouette over Belfast Harbour. The event marked the anniversary of Titanic's departure from the city's shipyards in 1912. This modern tribute blended history and technology, reminding viewers of the ship's enduring legacy.

They asserted the family's constitutional right to perform last rites, even as a magisterial inquiry is underway. Legislators also called for a judicial probe and a government statement on the incident.

stories.title: Jammu & Kashmir opens higher education for private sector
stories.summary: Jammu and Kashmir's assembly has greenlit a bill to establish private universities, a move hailed as historic. Education Minister Sakeena Itoo stated this will significantly enhance higher education access for local students and bolster the region's economy by retaining talent. The legislation also aims to ensure quality and student protection within these new institutions.

stories.title: Sam Pepper faces animal abuse claims after livestream clip with pet squirrel Potato draws heavy backlash online
stories.summary: Sam Pepper is facing backlash after a livestream clip showed him grabbing and shouting at his pet squirrel, Potato. The video, shared on Reddit, led to many accusing him of animal abuse. Pepper responded by calling it discipline and denied wrongdoing. The situation has sparked debate online, with his past controversies also being brought up again.

stories.title: Trump’s Xi moment? A military purge unfolds in the US
stories.summary: US President Trump's administration has overseen a significant churn in senior US military leadership, with multiple high-ranking officers exiting their posts. These removals, including Army Chief of Staff Gen Randy George, have raised concerns about institutional continuity and operational decision-making amid ongoing conflicts. The administration frames these changes as streamlining efforts, though critics question the impact on experienced leadership.

stories.title: Twitch streamer Emiru shares shocking middle school bullying moment as livestream with Cinna takes an unexpected emotional turn
stories.summary: Emiru opened up about being bullied in school during a livestream with Cinna on April 3, 2026. She shared painful memories, including a hurtful comment about her appearance and teasing about her ears. Cinna also shared her own story. The conversation mixed emotion with light moments, giving viewers a real look into their past experiences.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu polls: Is there any space for Vijay's TVK in the duopoly between DMK-AIADMK?
stories.summary: Actor Vijay Thalapathy's new party, TVK, is emerging as a third option in Tamil Nadu politics, challenging the long-standing dominance of DMK and AIADMK. With populist welfare promises and a strong social media presence, TVK aims to capture the significant unaligned vote, though electoral history suggests challenges remain.

stories.title: Battle of the 'tea state': High-stakes showdown in Gogoi's Jorhat and Sarma's Jalukbari fortress
stories.summary: Assam's 2026 Assembly elections are set for a defining clash, pitting the ruling NDA against a resurgent Congress. Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma faces a challenge in his Jalukbari stronghold, while Congress leader Gaurav Gogoi has turned Jorhat into a high-stakes battleground. The outcome will shape the state's political future.

stories.title: Raghav Chadha vs AAP: Rift between 'ghatak' MP and Kejriwal's 'soldiers' turns ugly — the showdown explained
stories.summary: Aam Aadmi Party MP Raghav Chadha has broken his silence after being removed as Rajya Sabha deputy leader. He denies allegations of 'soft PR' and deviating from the party line. Chadha states his silence should not be mistaken for defeat. He challenges his party to provide evidence for their claims. The controversy has drawn reactions from political opponents.

stories.title: Is Donald Trump’s triumphal tone on Iran facing a reality check?
stories.summary: President Trump's claims of 'decimating' Iran are challenged by two US warplane losses. Allies are distancing themselves, with France and Britain focusing on reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's actions are deepening economic fallout by disrupting oil flows. Diplomatic efforts continue amidst regional escalations.

These sessions focus on controlled, functional movements in urban spaces, helping seniors navigate daily life with renewed independence and energy. The trend reflects Singapore's aging population and promotes active aging by reducing fall risks and enhancing mobility.

PM Modi cautioned Congress's Iran conflict remarks could endanger Indians abroad, as Trump reportedly eyes a wider Cabinet reshuffle due to escalating pressures.

stories.title: 'All they care about is politics and power': PM Modi slams Congress for endangering Indians in Gulf
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi accused Congress leaders of endangering Indians in the Middle East with their remarks amid the US-Iran conflict. He stated that Congress's statements risk angering Gulf countries, potentially jeopardizing the safety of lakhs of Keralites working there. Modi emphasized his commitment to their security, highlighting India's strong relations with Gulf governments who consider Indians as family.

stories.title: 'BJP to take away Lakshmi Bhandar money': CM Mamata to woman voters in Bengal
stories.summary: West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee has warned women voters against sharing bank details with BJP workers, alleging a plot to commit financial fraud and steal benefits like Lakshmi Bhandar. She also criticized the Congress for a lack of coordination on electoral issues and failing to stand with the people during difficult times.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: The big Annamalai question — what BJP gains, what it risks

His decision, accepted by the leadership, allows him a broader organizational role, aiming to boost NDA candidates' prospects.

stories.title: Trump mulls big Cabinet shake-up as Iran war backlash deepens: Report
stories.summary: US President Trump is reportedly considering a significant Cabinet reshuffle amid growing concerns over the Iran war's political fallout and rising fuel prices. Frustration over falling approval ratings and midterm election anxieties are fueling discussions about replacing senior officials, including intelligence chief Tulsi Gabbard and commerce secretary Howard Lutnick. The administration faces pressure to project strength and address economic worries.

stories.title: Puducherry polls: Over 40% candidates are 'crorepatis'; how big is the wealth gap
stories.summary: Puducherry's assembly elections reveal a significant presence of wealthy candidates, with 41% declaring assets over Rs 1 crore. Jose Charles Martin leads with over Rs 609 crore, highlighting a stark wealth disparity. This trend shows a notable increase in crorepatis compared to previous elections, with major parties fielding a high proportion of affluent contestants.

stories.title: Projectile from US-Israeli strike hits near Iran’s only functioning nuclear facility in Bushehr
stories.summary: A security staff member died and a building was damaged after a projectile hit near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant on Saturday. This is the fourth incident targeting the facility since the conflict began. The International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed the strike. Iranian authorities stated the plant's core infrastructure remains unaffected and electricity production continues without disruption.

stories.title: 'Ghayal hoon isliye ghatak hoon': Raghav Chadha tears into AAP allegations with Dhurandhar reference

He denied claims of not joining opposition walkouts, refusing to sign an impeachment motion, and raising "trivial issues." Chadha asserted he has consistently raised significant public concerns in Parliament over his four-year tenure.

stories.title: Why Trump’s ‘God Squad’ decision to expand oil drilling in Gulf of Mexico is a vote for a whale’s extinction
stories.summary: A federal decision, approved upon the request of the Trump administration, to expand Gulf oil drilling has heightened fears of extinction for the critically endangered Rice’s whale, with fewer than 50 individuals remaining. Scientists note the species already lost over 20% of its population after the Deepwater Horizon spill, warning that renewed industrial activity could push it beyond recovery and erase one of the ocean’s rarest whales.

stories.title: Iran downs F-15, A-10 jets: First US combat aircraft losses in over 20 years

stories.summary: An American A-10 Thunderbolt II jet crashed into the Strait of Hormuz shortly after an F-15E Strike Eagle was reportedly shot down over Iran. The A-10's pilot was safely rescued, though details surrounding the crash remain scarce.

stories.summary: In a significant maritime achievement, an Indian LPG tanker has successfully maneuvered through the strategic Strait of Hormuz, flanked by six compatriots that have already reached Indian shores. However, the tension persists as seventeen Indian vessels, two of which are LPG carriers, hold position on the western side, biding their time for a chance to make the journey.

stories.title: Special session a violation of election code, claims Congress
stories.summary: The Congress party has criticized the BJP's recently announced 'special session', accusing it of violating campaign regulations, particularly regarding the contentious women's quota bill, which they claim is aimed at influencing voters in Tamil Nadu and Bengal. They express concern over proposed adjustments to parliamentary seats, warning it could marginalize smaller states and exacerbate regional inequalities.

stories.summary: The government plans to reconvene Parliament for a special session to pass women's reservation legislation for 2029. Despite opposition parties questioning the timing and motives, they've largely supported the proposal itself. The NDA is confident due to broad past support and women's growing influence as voters, anticipating passage of key bills.

stories.title: ‘Game changer’: England town stopped mowing 8 miles of grass and nature came back instantly while saving £25,000 a year
stories.summary: Rotherham town stopped mowing roadside grass and planted wildflowers. This policy change saved the town £25,000 annually. Wildlife returned in noticeable numbers. The verges transformed into colourful corridors of life. This initiative is now a model for cities seeking cost savings and biodiversity support. It shows how simple changes can yield significant environmental benefits.

stories.title: India’s third home-grown N-sub commissioned; Rajnath also launches stealth frigate, large cavitation tunnel facility at Vizag
stories.summary: India's naval strength significantly bolstered with the commissioning of INS Aridhaman, its third indigenous nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine, enhancing its second-strike capability. The vessel boasts advanced stealth and increased missile capacity. Additionally, the stealth frigate INS Taragiri was inducted, alongside the foundation stone laid for a crucial naval research facility, underscoring India's growing maritime prowess and self-reliance.

stories.title: Won’t be cowed, says Raghav, AAP brass says he indulged in ‘soft PR’
stories.summary: After Raghav Chadha's ousting as deputy leader in the Rajya Sabha, AAP leaders launched an intense critique, branding him as overly focused on superficial publicity while neglecting critical party ideologies. His peers challenged his muted stance on urgent political affairs and his conspicuous lack of presence at protests, suggesting a possible intimidation by PM Modi.

stories.title: “Those flirty texts”: Perez Hilton reacts as Prince Harry resurfaced chats with journalist raise concerns for Meghan Markle
stories.summary: Prince Harry’s old flirty messages with journalist Charlotte Griffiths have come out during his court case against Associated Newspapers. The chats, from 2011–2012, have sparked reactions, including from Perez Hilton. Reports say Meghan Markle is upset as the messages go public. Prince Harry has said he ended contact after learning Griffiths was a journalist. The court decision is still pending.

stories.title: Government moves to end toll waiver on ID display; no cash at booths from April 10

Exempted individuals must now use special FASTags or annual passes to prevent misuse and reduce arguments at toll plazas, paving the way for signal-free tolling.

stories.title: Supreme Court judge recuses self from case after reserving verdict
stories.summary: In a surprising twist, Justice K.V. Viswanathan of the Supreme Court opted to recuse himself from a case that had reached the judgment reservation stage. Upon reflection, he realized his prior role in representing the petitioner, Alchemist Asset Reconstruction Company, throughout his distinguished legal career.

stories.title: Government hopes to clear 5 crore pending cases with Jan Vishwas Bill
stories.summary: Government departments and prosecutors are urged to withdraw cases involving minor offences following the Jan Vishwas Bill's passage. This initiative aims to resolve millions of pending court cases by replacing jail terms with penalties for procedural lapses, particularly in healthcare. Serious offences remain under strict legal purview, offering relief for past minor violations.

stories.title: Supreme Court upholds harsher punishment for higher authority
stories.summary: The Supreme Court ruled that higher rank officials face harsher penalties for service misdeeds due to increased responsibility. Upholding differential punishments for bank employees involved in misappropriating funds, the apex court reinstated a senior manager's sacking, while an officer faced forced retirement and a gunman a salary cut. Courts must exercise restraint in interfering with disciplinary actions.

stories.title: MeT forecasts heavy rains in Kashmir plains, snowfall in higher reaches

Erratic weather conditions are expected to persist until April 10.

Fortunately, no injuries or property damage have been reported thus far in this developing situation.

stories.title: 10 ‘superpowers’ women possess that are biologically impossible for men
stories.summary: The woman's body is often thought of as simply an average body. From how the brain interprets sensory information all the way down to having two sets of immune system genes on its X chromosome (which accounts for the fact that females, on average, have a higher immunity to disease than males), a great number of characteristics that make females biologically unique do not get recognised. Here are some examples of physiological accomplishments performed by women with much greater levels of efficiency than men.

In this photo story, we take a look at how the crew and rocket got to this point of being ready to launch by looking back at all the hard work and challenges that occurred during the uncrewed Artemis 1 foundations in 2022, through the high-pressure survival training of the crews and the complex hardware integration in 2026.
